attempts.paper_title: Preconfigured dynamics in the hippocampus are guided by embryonic birthdate and rate of neurogenesis
attempts.entry_title: Birthdated CA1 pyramidal neurons in freely moving mice (Huszar et al. 2022)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Huszar, Zhang, Blockus and Buzsaki (2022) that can be tested on dandiset 000552, which holds sleep states, sharp-wave ripples, spike-sorted units and position from 17 mice electroporated at E13.5 to E16.5. It checks the description of the dataset and tests the findings on all pyramidal neurons on familiar and novel mazes (population-vector decorrelation, firing rates, spatial information and ratemap correlations). The units carry no light-responsiveness label and no optogenetic pulse times are stored, so the comparisons of same- and different-birthdate neurons are blocked.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Huszar et al. (2022) from dandiset 000552

outcomes.statement: Chronic recordings were made from 17 adult mice (12 males, 5 females) electroporated at E13.5 (n = 4), E14.5 (n = 3), E15.5 (n = 6) and E16.5 (n = 4).
outcomes.source: Results, first section; Methods, Implantation and recording
outcomes.notes: 17 mice, with E13.5 4, E14.5 3, E15.5 6 and E16.5 4, as the paper states. With each mouse's sex taken from most of its files, 12 males and 5 females, as the paper states. The sex field differs between files of two mice (e13_1f1 Female in 3 files and Male in 2; e13_1m1 Male in 9 and Female in 3), so reading only each mouse's first file gives 13 and 4. The ids, which carry f or m, also give 12 and 5.
deviations: The criterion took sex from the subject metadata without saying how to combine files that disagree; the value in most of a mouse's files is used, chosen after the per-file values were seen (the first round of this attempt read the first file and gave 13 and 4).

outcomes.statement: The recordings comprise 92 sessions lasting 113.7 to 475.6 min (median 309.1 min), each including a homecage period of sleep and wake.
outcomes.notes: 104 processed files, within 10% of the 96 sessions of Figure 1e and Figure 7f but not of the 92 of the Methods. Median duration 319.6 min (paper 309.1), range 113.7 to 494.2 min, all inside the widened range of 102.3 to 523.2 min; two files last exactly the paper's bounds (113.7 and 475.6 min). Without e15_13f1 and e16_3m2 there are 96 sessions with per-birthdate counts equal to Figure 1e (30, 24, 24, 18), range 113.7 to 475.6 min and median 309.9 min. Two files of e13_1f1 (200305, 200307) hold one Awake interval for the whole session and no scored sleep, so the statement that each session includes sleep fails for them; that part makes the outcome partial.
deviations: Session duration is the end of the last sleep-state or ripple interval; in 57 files the last spike falls 1.2 to 5.2 s later.

The criterion named the sleep condition without saying which outcome its failure gives; with the count, median and range holding and the sleep condition failing in 2 of 104 files, the outcome is taken as partial.
The session count was judged under two readings (92 and 96), as the paper gives both.

outcomes.statement: SPW-Rs were detected with duration limits of 20 to 200 ms, and their median duration across all recordings was 36.4 ms.
outcomes.notes: Median duration 36.0 ms over all 494,578 ripples pooled and 36.0 ms as the median of the 104 session medians (paper 36.4). All ripples last 20.0 to 199.2 ms, within the 20 to 200 ms limits. Per-mouse medians run from 29.6 to 40.0 ms.
deviations: Uses the ripples stored in the files; detection was not repeated.

outcomes.statement: The dataset includes 9,471 well-isolated units, 7,411 putative pyramidal cells and 2,060 putative interneurons.
outcomes.source: Methods, Unit isolation and classification; Extended Data Figure 2a
outcomes.notes: 8,201 units in 65 of 104 files, below the tolerance of 8,524 to 10,418. Six mice (e13_1f1, e13_1m1, e14_1m1, e15_4m1, e15_4m2, e15_5m1; 39 files) have no units. Files with units hold 34 to 376 (median 99). The 5 Hz rule classes 87.8% as putative pyramidal cells, against the paper's 78.3%.
deviations: The pyramidal fraction uses a firing-rate rule, as the files hold no cell type.

outcomes.statement: Nine mice (E13.5 n = 2, E14.5 n = 2, E15.5 n = 2, E16.5 n = 3) ran a spatial alternation task on a familiar figure-eight maze, and a cohort of three mice also explored novel environments.
outcomes.source: Results, SBD pyramidal neurons exhibit overlapping place tuning; Methods, Behavior
outcomes.notes: 11 mice have figure-eight trials. Under reading (b), the maze mice without e15_13f1 and e16_3m2 are nine, at E13.5 2, E14.5 2, E15.5 2 and E16.5 3, and three mice (e13_26m1, e15_13f1, e16_3m2) have novel recordings, so e13_26m1 is in both cohorts. Reading (a), disjoint cohorts of 12 mice, does not hold.
deviations: The paper calls the novel cohort separate; the reading that matches takes the overlap from the paper's code, recorded as an ambiguity.

outcomes.statement: On the figure-eight maze each trial was 205 cm long, position was tracked at 30 Hz, and animals ran at least ten trials along each arm in every session.
outcomes.notes: Median trial length 204.1 cm and tracking at 30.00 Hz in all 65 familiar recordings, both within tolerance. Only 38 of 65 sessions have at least ten trials on each visited arm (22 of 65 by expected arm), and 6 sessions have fewer than 20 trials (fewest 12), so neither the full nor the partial condition holds. The requirement may have applied to training, not to every recorded session.
deviations: Two readings of "trials along each arm" (visited and expected) were used; neither holds.

outcomes.statement: The novel-environment cohort of three mice made 16 novel environment explorations in six distinct environments (two linear tracks, three open fields and one figure-eight maze).
outcomes.source: Results, SBD pyramidal neurons exhibit overlapping place tuning; Methods, Behavior
outcomes.notes: Three mice with 9 novel explorations that have trials and position (3 T-maze runs of about 164 cm, 3 linear-track runs of 110 cm and 3 of 100 cm), against 16. The novel-cohort sessions also hold 7 epochs of 10 to 50 min without position that are not a session's last epoch, and the files hold no other position or video series for them. They are not counted; they would bring the count to 16, but they were picked after the data were seen and nothing in the files marks them as explorations. No open field has position.

outcomes.statement: Population firing-rate vectors at the same linearized position decorrelate between left and right trials once the animal leaves the common stem of the figure-eight maze (median correlations stem 0.93, turn 1 0.412, arm 0.372, turn 2 0.394).
outcomes.notes: 57 sessions of nine mice (the paper's bin counts, 4,218 stem bins, imply the same 57), with 28 to 242 putative pyramidal cells per session. Kruskal-Wallis H = 7632.7 (paper 7278.3), p = 0, stem highest. Stem 0.937 is within tolerance; turn 1 0.547, arm 0.492 and turn 2 0.465 are above the paper's 0.412, 0.372 and 0.394. The stem is the most correlated segment in every mouse. The medians depend strongly on the cell rule; at most 2 Hz gives 0.925, 0.387, 0.288, 0.306; at most 10 Hz gives 0.966, 0.787, 0.771, 0.746; all units 0.988, 0.948, 0.94, 0.921; no speed threshold 0.924, 0.589, 0.522, 0.492. With a 2.59 Hz rule, which classes the paper's fraction of units (0.783) as pyramidal, the medians are 0.928, 0.436, 0.343 and 0.357, all four within tolerance; the criterion fixed the 5 Hz rule, so this variant does not change the outcome. 51 of 11,685 bins had no value.
deviations: Putative pyramidal cells by session mean rate (at most 5 Hz), not by waveform and autocorrelogram; the files hold no cell type or waveforms.
Speed from smoothed linearized position, not a Kalman filter.

outcomes.statement: Individual pyramidal neurons preserve their theta-related firing rates between the familiar and novel environments (Spearman rho = 0.7378, n = 2,544 neurons).
outcomes.notes: Spearman rho = 0.726 over 2,038 putative pyramidal cells with a familiar and a novel rate (paper 0.7378 over 2,544), p = 0; per mouse 0.711 to 0.745, per session 0.586 to 0.826. Variants with all units, a 10 Hz rule or a 1.5 cm/s running threshold give 0.754 to 0.802. 679 cells of the 3 sessions without a novel maze have no novel rate. The running rate now ends each running stretch at the end of its trial (round 1 gave 0.734 with stretches that could span the gap between trials).
deviations: The rate is the firing rate while running at 5 cm/s or faster inside maze trials, in place of the rate in LFP theta cycles; the LFP is in the raw files of 8 of the 9 novel sessions but was not used.
Novel mazes are only those with position; the open fields are not in the data.
Putative pyramidal cells by firing rate.

outcomes.statement: Pairwise spatial ratemap correlations between pyramidal neurons are higher in novel environments (median 0.048) than in the familiar environment (median -0.045).
outcomes.notes: Median familiar -0.0530 over 327,656 pairs (within tolerance) and novel -0.0364 over 242,655 pairs (outside 0.018 to 0.078); rank-sum p = 0.67. Within each of the 9 sessions with a novel maze the novel median is higher than the familiar one (sign test p = 0.0039; rank-sum p < 0.05 within 7 of the 9 sessions), so the direction holds session by session; the pooled test, which the criterion names, is weighted by the sessions with most pairs; with familiar pairs only from those sessions the pooled test gives p = 0.1. Variants with all units (p = 0.38) or a 10 Hz rule (p = 0.66) agree; including the stem gives p = 3.5e-50 with novel higher. Per maze kind, novel medians run from -0.0548 to 0.0073.
deviations: All pairs of putative pyramidal cells, where the paper's pairs each include a light-responsive neuron (not identifiable in the files).
Novel mazes are only the T-maze and linear tracks with position; the paper's novel pairs also come from open fields with two-dimensional maps.

outcomes.statement: Spatial information is lower in novel environments than in the familiar one (median 0.39 against 0.88 bits/s).
outcomes.notes: Familiar median 0.631 bits/s over 2,709 cells and novel 0.270 over 2,028 cell-maze values, rank-sum p = 1.5e-59, so information is lower in novel mazes as stated, but both medians are below the tolerances (0.792 to 0.968 and 0.351 to 0.429). The code's unweighted measure gives 0.646 and 0.285. By mouse, familiar 0.617 to 0.645; novel 0.083 to 0.337 on linear tracks and 0.282 to 0.608 on the T-maze.
deviations: Skaggs information over left and right maps of the whole linearized track, with putative pyramidal cells by firing rate; no open fields.

outcomes.statement: Theta-related firing rates are slightly lower in novel environments than in the familiar one (median 0.69 against 0.77 Hz).
outcomes.notes: Familiar median 0.794 Hz over 2,717 cells and novel 0.714 Hz over 2,038, both within tolerance of the paper's 0.77 and 0.69 Hz; rank-sum p = 0.041 (paper 3.3e-3). The difference is weak. The paired signed-rank test gives a median ratio of 0.942, p = 0.19; familiar from the sessions with a novel maze only gives p = 0.09; the variants (all units, 10 Hz rule, 1.5 cm/s threshold) give lower novel rates with p = 0.075 to 0.11. Novel is lower in two mice (0.722 against 0.883, 0.680 against 0.835) and slightly higher in e15_13f1 (0.734 against 0.729). Round 1 gave 0.958 and 0.799 Hz, p = 7e-06, with running stretches that could span the gap between trials and count its spikes but not its time; in 371 of 698 pairs of consecutive trials the animal was running at the end of one and the start of the next.
deviations: Running rate in place of the rate in LFP theta cycles.
Putative pyramidal cells by firing rate; no open fields.

outcomes.statement: 664 of 7,411 putative pyramidal neurons (8.96%) were light-responsive, that is, birthdated.
outcomes.notes: No unit is labelled light-responsive and no optogenetic pulse times are stored in the processed or raw files (stimulus and acquisition are empty in the processed files; a listing of every dataset in all 13 raw files finds only the ElectricalSeries, the LFP and the electrodes table). The paper's labels come from CellExplorer optoTag fields and pulses.events.mat files on the lab server, which the paper's data link reaches only through the lab databank and Globus, at no pinned identifier. The Methods say the pulses were given at the end of each session, in blocks of five 200 ms apart, and that the raw data were clipped out from 0.15 ms before to 0.8 ms after each pulse; they give no interval between blocks and do not say what the clipped samples hold. In the raw file of e16_3m2_211213 the wideband signal ends 2 s after the processed session, and ten 2 s windows over its last 30 min hold no flat or zeroed stretch on eight channels; if clipped samples are flat or zero, the stimulation period is not in the deposited recording. The other 10 wideband files (54 to 184 GB each) were not scanned.

outcomes.statement: The fraction of light-responsive pyramidal cells per session follows a bell-shaped wave over birthdates, peaking at E15.5 (E13.5 5.39%, E14.5 11.16%, E15.5 14.74%, E16.5 9.16%; ANOVA p = 4e-4).
outcomes.notes: Needs the light-responsive units of each session; see ed2-light-responsive-count.

outcomes.statement: Neurons born on later days lie more superficially in the pyramidal layer (median normalized depth 0.71, 0.48, 0.28 and 0.19 for E13.5 to E16.5).
outcomes.notes: Histology (tdTomato and DAPI images) is not in the dandiset and was not found elsewhere.

outcomes.statement: Earlier-born light-responsive neurons more often shift their preferred theta phase in REM sleep (30.89% at E13.5 to 19.7% at E16.5; regression slope -3.42% per day).
outcomes.notes: Needs light-responsive units by birthdate; see ed2-light-responsive-count. It also needs the LFP, which is in the raw files of only 12 sessions.

outcomes.statement: Earlier-born light-responsive pyramidal neurons have higher firing rates (medians 1.57, 1.63, 1.62 and 1.16 Hz; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.016).
outcomes.notes: Needs the light-responsive units; see ed2-light-responsive-count. Grouping all units by the mouse's birthdate would test a different quantity, as most units in a mouse are not birthdated.

outcomes.statement: Burst index is an inverted-U function of birthdate (medians 0.1167, 0.1272, 0.136, 0.1082; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.0044).
outcomes.notes: Needs the light-responsive units; see ed2-light-responsive-count.

outcomes.statement: Same-birthdate (SBD) pairs fire more synchronously than different-birthdate (DBD) pairs in 11 of 13 animals.
outcomes.notes: SBD and DBD pairs cannot be formed without light-responsiveness labels; six of the homecage mice also have no units.

outcomes.statement: SBD pairs cofire more than DBD pairs in theta cycles (median 0.0189 against 0.0087).
outcomes.notes: Needs SBD and DBD pairs (no labels) and theta cycles from the LFP (raw files of 12 sessions only).

outcomes.statement: Intermediate-birthdate neurons have lower theta depth modulation in waking but not in REM sleep.
outcomes.notes: Needs light-responsive units by birthdate and the LFP.

outcomes.statement: SPW-R firing rates and participation of light-responsive neurons are an inverted-U function of birthdate.
outcomes.notes: Needs light-responsive units by birthdate; the ripples themselves are in the files.

outcomes.statement: SBD pairs cofire more than DBD pairs in SPW-Rs (median 0.0399 against 0.0231).
outcomes.notes: Needs SBD and DBD pairs; no labels.

outcomes.statement: Assembly members cofire more in SPW-Rs than member-nonmember pairs, and segregation from nonmembers depends nonlinearly on the members' birthdate.
outcomes.notes: The member-nonmember part could be computed, but the analysis keeps only assemblies with a light-responsive member and groups them by birthdate, which needs the labels.

outcomes.statement: Assemblies with intermediate-birthdate members are expressed in SPW-Rs at higher rates (E13.5 8.16, E14.5 9.25, E15.5 8.16, E16.5 6.9 Hz; ANOVA p = 0.0158).
outcomes.notes: Assemblies are grouped by the birthdate of light-responsive members; no labels.

outcomes.statement: A model with a bell-shaped rate of neurogenesis and correlations among SBD neurons reproduces the assembly expression rates, and a uniform-neurogenesis model does not.
outcomes.notes: The model is fitted to the assembly expression rates of fig3e-assembly-expression, which is blocked.

outcomes.statement: Spatial information and coverage on the maze are largest in intermediate-birthdate neurons.
outcomes.notes: Needs light-responsive units by birthdate.

outcomes.statement: SBD pairs have higher spatial ratemap correlations than DBD pairs on the familiar maze (median 0.0152 against -0.0256).
outcomes.notes: Needs SBD and DBD pairs; no labels.

outcomes.statement: The ratemap overlap of SBD pairs depends on their anatomical distance, larger within 250 micrometres.
outcomes.notes: Needs SBD pairs and the shank of each unit; units have no electrode link and their group_id does not match the electrode groups in 64 of 65 files.

outcomes.statement: Between left and right trials, ratemaps of SBD pairs reorganize closer together than those of DBD pairs.
outcomes.notes: Needs SBD and DBD pairs; no labels.

outcomes.statement: In novel environments SBD pairs have higher ratemap correlations than DBD pairs (median 0.117 against 0.046).
outcomes.notes: Needs SBD and DBD pairs; no labels.

outcomes.statement: Ratemaps of SBD pairs remain closer together than those of DBD pairs between the familiar and novel environments.
outcomes.notes: Needs SBD and DBD pairs; no labels.

outcomes.statement: SBD pyramidal pairs converge onto the same interneurons more than DBD pairs (median convergence 0.2727 against 0.2).
outcomes.notes: Needs SBD pairs and putative interneurons; neither labels nor cell types are in the files.

outcomes.statement: Convergence onto interneurons and spike transmission probability are bell-shaped functions of the presynaptic neurons' birthdate.
outcomes.notes: Needs light-responsive units by birthdate and putative interneurons.

outcomes.statement: Of all pyramidal pairs, 65.27% share at least one postsynaptic interneuron, and cofiring in SPW-Rs, theta cycles and ratemap overlap all increase with convergence.
outcomes.notes: Uses all pyramidal-interneuron pairs and needs no birthdate labels. The notebook applies the rate rule (units above 5 Hz as interneurons, 1,001 in all against the paper's 2,060) and the connection test of the Methods (0.8 ms CCG bins, hollowed-Gaussian baseline of 15 ms s.d., alpha 0.001) to two sessions. In e15_13f1_220117, whose mouse is not among the 15 of Figure 7f, the test at fixed lags of 0.8 to 3.2 ms detects connections in 5,073 of 11,319 possible pairs (0.448, against 31,932 of 184,230 or 0.173 in the paper), and 96.7% of pyramidal pairs share a target (paper 65.27%). In e13_26m1_211019, inside the Figure 7f cohort, it detects 0.407, with 96.7% of pairs sharing a target. The Methods test the three bins around the CCG peak, where this test uses fixed lags; a peak-centred variant (peak sought at lags up to 4.0 ms, a range the Methods do not give, chosen after the fixed-lag results were seen) detects 0.405 and 0.394, with 95.7% and 93.4% of pairs sharing a target. With a connection rate this far from the paper's under both forms, the procedure differs from the paper's, whose connections come from the lab's CellExplorer mono_res files (not public; the paper's code reads them and does not compute them). The difference may lie in this implementation as well as in what the Methods leave unstated (lag range, hollow fraction, CCG window). Of the paper's 96 sessions (the files without e15_13f1 and e16_3m2), 39 have no units in the dandiset, and cofiring in theta cycles needs the LFP, which the processed files lack.

findings.statement: No unit is labelled light-responsive (birthdated), and no optogenetic pulse times are stored in the processed or the raw files, so the paper's comparisons of same- and different-birthdate neurons and its birthdate profiles (22 of the 35 claims listed here) cannot be tested. The labels exist in the lab's CellExplorer files (optoTag, putativeCellType), which are not public at a pinned identifier.
Units carry no putative cell type and no waveforms, though the paper classifies 7,411 pyramidal cells and 2,060 interneurons.

Six of the 17 mice (e13_1f1, e13_1m1, e14_1m1, e15_4m1, e15_4m2, e15_5m1; 39 files) have sleep states and ripples but no units and no position. The dandiset holds 8,201 units where the paper reports 9,471.

Of the 16 novel environment explorations, only 9 have position and trials, and no open field has position. The novel-cohort sessions hold 7 further epochs of 10 to 50 min without position or video that may be the missing explorations.

The subject sex differs between files of the same mouse. e13_1f1 is Female in 3 files and Male in 2; e13_1m1 is Male in 9 and Female in 3. The value in most of each mouse's files gives the paper's 12 males and 5 females.
The trials column is_familiar_maze is True only for the first two trials of sessions with a single maze recording, where every trial is on the familiar maze (112 True, 1,182 False).
In several novel recordings (e13_26m1 211019, 211116, 211119; e15_13f1 220120; e16_3m2 211213) x and y lie between 0 and 1 though stated in cm.
Twelve of the 13 raw files give a session start of 2011-08-18 for sessions recorded in 2021 and 2022.
The processed file of e16_3m1_210201 holds a copy of the 1250 Hz LFP of the raw file, labelled with a rate of 30,000 Hz and a conversion factor of 3.05e-13 V.

Units have no link to the electrodes table, and their group_id values ("Group3") do not match the electrode group names ("Group 3") in 64 of 65 files, so a unit's shank and position on the probe cannot be recovered.
The embryonic day of electroporation, the variable the paper is about, is stored only as the prefix of each subject id (e13 for E13.5); the age is given as P3M/P6M for every mouse.
Two files of e13_1f1 (200305, 200307) hold a single Awake interval for the whole session, so sleep was not scored, though both hold ripples.

Only 38 of 65 familiar-maze sessions have ten or more trials on each visited arm, and 6 have fewer than 20 trials, where the Methods require ten per arm in every session; 19 of 1,942 trials have no start or stop time.

The Methods give 92 sessions, while Figure 1e (30, 24, 24 and 18 sessions) and Figure 7f give 96. The dandiset's files of the 15 homecage mice are 96 sessions that match Figure 1e by birthdate and the Methods' duration bounds exactly (113.7 to 475.6 min).
The paper calls the novel-environment cohort of three mice separate, but one of them (e13_26m1) is also among the nine figure-eight mice, in the dandiset and in the paper's code.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper's full text (the PMC author manuscript). The verifier tested helper functions on synthetic inputs and queried the archive's asset metadata for the blocked claims. Its report gave its own outcome for each claim; it agreed with the record on 34 of 35 outcomes, gave reproduced for cohort-birthdates, and for fig7fg-convergence-cofiring agreed on blocked but disputed the reason. Problems B6 (dependent bins and pairs treated as independent, as in the paper), B8 (skaggs_information weights by unsmoothed occupancy and divides by smoothed occupancy) and B9 (mean_rates divides by an end time 1 to 5 s short of the last spike in 57 files) it marked as not affecting a conclusion; they were left as they are, since the first follows the paper, the second follows the Methods' map definition with the occupancy probability of Skaggs et al., and the third changes rates by under 0.1%.

disagreements.reason: 17 mice and the birthdate counts 4/3/6/4 match. The notebook's 13 M / 4 F comes from taking each mouse's first file. The sex field differs between files of the same mouse; e13_1f1 is Male in 2 files and Female in 3, e13_1m1 is Male in 9 and Female in 3 (cell 7, and the DANDI asset metadata it queried). Taking each mouse's majority gives 12 M / 5 F, which matches. Problem B2 (affects a conclusion) is the same point.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook after the round-1 revision, with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper's full text (the PMC10807234 author manuscript). The verifier agreed with all 35 outcomes, and for fig7fg-convergence-cofiring accepted the block while calling two parts of its reasoning weak. It quoted five sentences the outputs do not support: the count of 31 sessions without units (39), the statement on stimulation channels in the raw files (1 of 13 listed), the assumption about clipped pulses in cell 16, a swapped column label in the fig6c output, and the reading of the T-maze as the novel figure-eight. Remaining points bearing on a conclusion were B4 (fig5e rate rule), the weak fig6d-rate test, fig7fg's single out-of-cohort session and detector, and B7 (raw files). The round-1 response on fig7fg also gave 31 sessions; it is left as recorded, and the notes are corrected.

attempts.paper_title: Spontaneous behaviour is structured by reinforcement without explicit reward
attempts.entry_title: Dopamine and spontaneous behaviour in mice (Markowitz, Gillis, Jay et al. 2023)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Markowitz, Gillis, Jay et al. (2023) on dandiset 000559, which holds the dLight photometry, MoSeq syllables and closed-loop optogenetic sessions of the paper. It relates DLS dopamine to velocity, syllable identity, syllable use and sequence entropy, compares DMS with DLS, and tests the reinforcement of target syllables by closed-loop dopamine release. The modelling of Figures 4 and 5 is not attempted.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Markowitz, Gillis, Jay et al. (2023) from dandiset 000559

outcomes.statement: DLS dopamine fluctuations are significantly negatively correlated with translational velocity at short timescales (under 10 s), and the correlation reverses and becomes positive at longer timescales, for both dLight transient rates and binned amplitudes.
outcomes.notes: Over 121 DLS sessions from 14 mice, binned dLight amplitude and transient rate are both significantly negatively correlated with 2D speed at all 20 timescales below 10 s (amplitude mean r -0.201 to -0.109, rate -0.123 to -0.062; shuffle ranges within about 0.02 of zero), and all 14 mice are negative at 0.25 s for both. The transient rate turns positive from 18.75 s and is significantly positive at 47 of 100 timescales of 10 s or more (largest 0.113 at 58.75 s). The binned amplitude is still significantly negative at 49.75 s and is significantly positive at none of the 100 longer timescales (largest 0.005). The claim holds for one of the two measures under both readings of "short timescales".
deviations: dLight is re-referenced and z-scored from the stored dF/F series; the paper used a pre-computed z-scored trace that is not in the files.
100 shuffles where the paper used 1,000.
121 sessions where the paper's code reports 216 for this panel; the dandiset holds fewer sessions, and habituation sessions are left out here.

outcomes.statement: Average syllable-associated dLight amplitudes differ across syllables (Kruskal-Wallis H = 209.29, P < 1e-25, n = 518 mouse-syllable pairs).
outcomes.notes: The 518 mouse-syllable pairs (14 mice x 37 syllables) match the paper's n. Kruskal-Wallis P = 5.98e-37, below the paper's 1e-25, but H = 266.40 is 27 % above 209.29 and outside the 10 % tolerance. Variants give H 266.99 (target instances kept), 268.58 (pairs with at least 50 instances) and 265.62 (the 9 DLS sessions failing the quality criteria added), so neither the quality filter nor the post-session rule explains the difference. Per-mouse tests are significant in 14 of 14 mice.
deviations: Instances from 177 DLS sessions without stimulation (habituation sessions left out); the paper used more sessions per mouse.

outcomes.statement: Random forest classifiers cannot predict which syllable is being expressed from the coincident dLight peak amplitude or waveform.
outcomes.notes: Held-out accuracy for 37 syllables is 0.0271 from peak amplitude and 0.0323 from the waveform and its derivative, 1.00 and 1.20 times chance (0.0270), below the criterion of 0.0541. Shuffled labels give 0.0278 and 0.0279.
deviations: A 100-tree sklearn random forest with at least 5 instances per leaf on 1,000 instances per syllable, where the paper used cuML with 1,000 trees; the paper gives no accuracy, so "unable to predict" was set as below twice chance.
One label shuffle per feature set as the null, where the paper used 100.

outcomes.statement: Syllables associated on average with more DLS dopamine in an experiment tend to be used more.
outcomes.notes: Over 507 mouse-syllable pairs in 14 mice, held-out r = 0.165 between syllable-associated dLight and syllable count; no shuffle of 200 reached it (P < 0.005, 95th percentile 0.051). Per-mouse rank correlations are positive in 14 of 14 mice. The paper's r is shown only in its figure.
deviations: Fivefold cross-validation repeated 20 times and 200 shuffles, where the paper used 100 repeats and 1,000 shuffles.

outcomes.statement: Mice string together less predictable sequences after syllables associated with more dopamine; average syllable-associated dLight correlates positively with the entropy of the syllable's outgoing transitions.
outcomes.notes: Held-out r = 0.271 between syllable-associated dLight and the entropy of outgoing transitions over 507 mouse-syllable pairs; no shuffle of 200 reached it (P < 0.005, 95th percentile 0.042). Positive in 14 of 14 mice.
deviations: Plain Shannon entropy of the outgoing transition probabilities per experiment, as the Methods state; the code uses a Dirichlet entropy estimate.

outcomes.statement: When an instance of a syllable coincides with a higher-amplitude dopamine transient, that syllable is used more over the following minutes.
outcomes.notes: The mean correlation between an instance's dLight and the count of the same syllable in the next n syllables is positive at every n (0.0043 to 0.0251) and significant from n = 10 to 90 (P < 0.01), 11 of 14 mice positive at n = 10. It is not significant at n = 110, 130, 150 and 170 (P = 0.09, 0.15, 0.18 and 0.05), so it holds at 6 of 10 values up to 190 and fails the criterion's "throughout"; it is significant again from 190 to 330. The shuffles permute only instances with a dLight peak, so the same groups enter the observed value and every shuffle (15,480 at n = 10).
deviations: Five equal time segments in place of the paper's five behavioural segments (Extended Data Fig. 2e).
Correlations are compared with shuffles directly, not z-scored to them; 100 shuffles.

outcomes.statement: dLight recordings in dorsomedial striatum (DMS) show less frequent dopamine transients than in DLS.
outcomes.source: Results, third section; Extended Data Figure 7a,b
outcomes.notes: DMS mice have a median 56.48 transients per minute against 62.12 in DLS (8 against 14 mice, U = 13, two-sided P = 0.0022); with a 1.96 threshold 22.10 against 25.21 (P = 0.0006).

outcomes.statement: DMS dopamine transients do not predict future syllable usage.
outcomes.source: Results, third section; Extended Data Figure 7
outcomes.notes: By the test used for fig2e-dlight-predicts-future-usage, DMS dLight predicts the later use of the same syllable. Mean r is 0.0110 to 0.0331 for n from 10 to 190, significant at 9 of those 10 values (n = 10 to 90 at P below 0.01), positive in 8 of 8 mice at n = 10, and larger than in DLS (0.0044 to 0.0251). The test is this attempt's version of the paper's (see the deviations of fig2e-dlight-predicts-future-usage). The paper's Extended Data Fig. 7 has no lagged future-usage test; it supports the claim with the encoding model (panel e) and the title "DMS dopamine does not correlate with syllable usage or entropy". The across-syllable count test of fig2b-dlight-usage-across-syllables run on DMS agrees with the paper (held-out r = 0.026, shuffle P = 0.170). That the lagged test finds DMS stronger than DLS suggests it differs from the paper's (equal time segments, no z-scoring to the shuffles); the outcome follows the pre-set criterion.
deviations: Same deviations as fig2e-dlight-predicts-future-usage.

outcomes.statement: Pairing a target syllable with optogenetic dopamine release (Opto-DA) increases its use relative to baseline more than in no-opsin controls (log2 fold change in target counts, one-sided Mann-Whitney U = 197, P = 0.002, f = 0.82).
outcomes.notes: 20 Opto-DA and 12 control mice, 191 targets. Log2 fold change in target counts, Opto-DA median 0.330, control 0.081; U = 198, one-sided P = 0.0013, f = 0.82 (paper 197, 0.002, 0.82).
deviations: Stimulation, baseline and post sessions are identified from stimulation pulses, session dates and descriptions, as the files give no session number or type.

outcomes.statement: The cumulative increase in target counts relative to baseline is larger in Opto-DA mice than in controls (one-sided Mann-Whitney U = 184, P = 0.007, f = 0.77).
outcomes.notes: Change in target counts, Opto-DA median 27.6, control -2.3; U = 182, one-sided P = 0.0083, f = 0.76 (paper 184, 0.007, 0.77).
deviations: As for fig3e-optoda-learning.

outcomes.statement: Only a fraction of Opto-DA mice learn; nine mice exceed the largest change in target counts of any control ("learners").
outcomes.source: Methods, "Quantifying changes in target syllable counts"; Figure 3e; Extended Data Figure 10
outcomes.notes: Seven of 20 Opto-DA mice exceed the largest control change (54.5, vta-nacc-ctrl-6), not nine. All seven are among the nine the paper's code printed; the other two (3442 at 47.3 and dls-ai32jr-1 at 41.7) fall below that control; their per-target changes range from -49 to 148 and -26 to 93, against -50 to 152 for vta-nacc-ctrl-6. Counting mice above the control maximum of the log2 fold change gives 10. The criterion is the count, which is outside the tolerance. The statement's first part, that only a fraction of mice learn, holds (7 of 20).

outcomes.statement: In learners, the change in target usage during stimulation predicts the change in the post-stimulation sessions (Pearson r = 0.89, P = 0.005).
outcomes.notes: Among the seven learners found here, r = 0.891 between the change during stimulation and in the post sessions (one-sided shuffle P = 0.017); with the code's nine learners r = 0.888 (P = 0.001). The learner set differs from the paper's (see fig3e-learner-count), and the result holds with either. Controls also correlate (r = 0.591, one-sided P = 0.017, two-sided 0.039), where the paper reports P = 0.082.

outcomes.statement: Brief (250 ms) Opto-DA does not change movement at the moment of stimulation; no comparison between stimulation and catch trials in any mouse is significant.
outcomes.notes: The test needs catch trials (target detections on which stimulation was withheld), which the files do not mark; the conversion kept only the stimulated detections. The criterion's substitute (online target onsets with no pulse in the next 0.5 s) is not the paper's catch set. The Methods give stimulation on 75 % of detections; with the substitute, stimulations are a median 0.593 of detections per mouse (0.521 to 0.687; 0.111 to 0.776 over sessions). It does not isolate the light's effect. In no-opsin controls, stimulation trials differ from these catch trials at P < 0.05 in 9 of 12 mice, and the controls' median difference (3.96 mm/s) exceeds the Opto-DA one (-0.07 mm/s; Opto-DA against control U = 68, P = 0.045). With catch trials at least 2 s from any pulse, controls are still significant in 9 of 12. Taken literally, the criterion gives 9 of 20 Opto-DA mice significant, which would be not reproduced (8 of 20 with the 2-s catch trials); because the controls fail, the claim is recorded as blocked.

outcomes.statement: Extending stimulation to 3 s (pulsed, 25 Hz) makes mice increase their velocity.
outcomes.source: Figure 3m; Extended Data Figure 10l; Results, fourth section
outcomes.notes: As for fig3l-no-kinematic-effect. With the criterion's substitute catch trials, stimulations are 0.302 to 0.348 of detections per mouse, and onsets during an ongoing 3-s train count as catch trials. 1 of the 3 Opto-DA mice with 3-s pulsed sessions is significant (P = 0.024; the others 0.091 and 0.053), which taken literally would be partially reproduced, and both controls are (P = 0.0002 and 0.0083), with larger differences (median 6.75 mm/s against 4.58). With catch trials at least 2 s from any pulse, 0 of 3 Opto-DA mice are significant (P = 0.10, 0.064, 0.082) and both controls still are (P = 0.0007 and 0.010). The 2-s continuous sessions give significant differences in 2 of 3 Opto-DA mice and 2 of 3 controls.

outcomes.statement: Spontaneous syllable-associated dopamine transients roughly match those during consumption of an unexpected chocolate chip (mean spontaneous peak 2.12 +- 0.80 z, n = 5,247; reward 2.36 +- 0.92 z, n = 10).
outcomes.notes: No session in the dandiset is described as a food-reward session, and the human-annotated consumption times are not in any file (session descriptions, NWB contents of the photometry files). The paper's code reads them from its Zenodo deposit (doi:10.5281/zenodo.7274803, one 60.8 GB zip), which was not opened here.

outcomes.statement: The average syllable-associated dLight transient exceeds that associated with movement initiation (P = 0.0006, n = 14 mice).
outcomes.notes: Not attempted in this attempt, for time. The data it needs (dLight, syllable labels, 2D speed for movement initiations) are in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: A higher-amplitude dopamine transient at a syllable instance is followed by less predictable syllable choices over the next several seconds.
outcomes.notes: Not attempted in this attempt, for time. The data it needs are in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Behavioural sequences right after Opto-DA stimulation are less predictable than after catch trials.
outcomes.notes: Not attempted; it compares stimulation with catch trials, which the files do not mark (see fig3l-no-kinematic-effect).

outcomes.statement: Opto-DA delivered on the fastest (slowest) quartile of target instances makes later instances faster (slower).
outcomes.source: Results, fourth section; Extended Data Figure 10d
outcomes.notes: Not attempted in this attempt, for time. The 94 velocity-conditioned files of 9 mice are in the dandiset, with "Stim Up" and "Stim Down" notes.

outcomes.statement: Per mouse, the influence of endogenous dopamine on syllable counts and on sequence entropy are correlated (r = 0.69, P = 0.001).
outcomes.notes: Not attempted in this attempt, for time; it builds on the per-mouse lagged analyses of Fig. 2e and 2k.

outcomes.statement: Mice whose syllable use is more influenced by endogenous dopamine learn more from Opto-DA (r = 0.51, P = 0.001).
outcomes.notes: Not attempted in this attempt, for time. The mice it needs have photometry and closed-loop sessions in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Syllables with higher endogenous dLight on catch trials are more reinforced by Opto-DA (r = 0.32, P < 0.001).
outcomes.notes: Not attempted; it uses dLight on catch trials, which the files do not mark.

outcomes.statement: A model in which endogenous and exogenous dopamine add predicts held-out syllable choices better than shuffled and noise controls (median r 0.20 against 0.04).
outcomes.source: Figure 4h; Methods, "Decoding model predicting behaviour from dLight"
outcomes.notes: Not attempted in this attempt, for time.

outcomes.statement: A Q-learning agent rewarded by syllable-associated dLight learns a transition matrix similar to the observed one, best when dopamine also transiently raises choice variability.
outcomes.notes: Not attempted in this attempt, for time; the paper fitted it on a 128-CPU machine, and its code is in the repository named under inputs.

findings.statement: The closed-loop files mark stimulation onsets but not catch trials (target detections on which stimulation was withheld); the conversion kept only the stimulated detections. Comparisons of stimulation with catch trials (Fig. 3i, 3l, 3m, 4f) cannot be made, and a substitute selection shows stimulation-catch differences in 9 of 12 no-opsin controls.

No file states the genotype or opsin of a mouse. Opto-DA (Ai32) and no-opsin control mice are told apart only by the stimulation site ("snc (axon)" or "ctrl"), and the dLight+ChrimsonR mice only by their subject names.

Session type (baseline, stimulation, post) and session number are not stored; they must be inferred from free-text descriptions, dates and stimulation pulses. Five files with stimulation are described as recording sessions.
Every closed-loop file states a 635-nm stimulator (Opto Engine MRL-III-635), including the Ai32 (ChR2) mice, which the Methods say were stimulated with 470-nm light.
The dLight-only mice (C57BL/6J in the Methods) carry the subject description "wild-type DAT-IRES-Cre and Ai32 mice", the same as the optogenetic mice.

In 28 photometry and 547 closed-loop files the syllable timestamps are not ascending. In 573 of these 575 the rows are rotated, with one backward step, which is at least 0.95 of the session length in 558 files and 0.635 of it at the least. Sorting by timestamp restores a regular 30-Hz clock (median interval 0.03337 s in every file).
Two closed-loop files of mouse 3155 store every syllable frame twice (53,822 and 53,862 repeated timestamps), and have two and three non-ascending steps.
14 files of dLight+ChrimsonR mice hold empty syllable series; all list two target syllables.

For the dLight+ChrimsonR mice only the 250-ms closed-loop sessions are present; the 2-s and pulsed sessions the Methods describe are not. The dandiset holds 224 DLS photometry files without stimulation (210 with syllables, 193 of them not habituation sessions, 177 of those passing the quality criteria), where the Methods give 379 experiments.
The food-reward sessions and the consumption times of Fig. 2a are not in the dandiset.

The dandiset includes behaviour-only files for photometry sessions without a dLight series (111 files, among them all files of dls-dlight-6, dls-dlight-8, dms-dlight-7 and dms-dlight-9) and sessions that fail the paper's quality criteria (16 DLS and 11 DMS), with no flag saying which were excluded from the paper.
The re-referenced, z-scored dLight trace used by every photometry analysis is not stored; it must be recomputed from the stored dF/F and smoothed reference, whose regression fit is not stored either.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: The executed notebook of the first run with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file. The header still listed which claims were tested and blocked.

It asked for the per-target stimulation and baseline counts and the chosen baseline day for these two mice and for vta-nacc-ctrl-6.

attempts.paper_title: Probing subthreshold dynamics of hippocampal neurons by pulsed optogenetics
attempts.entry_title: Pulsed optogenetics in hippocampal CA1 (Valero et al. 2022)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Valero, Zutshi, Yoon and Buzsaki (2022) on dandiset 000568, which holds 28 sessions of CA1 units recorded with uLED probes in four CaMKIIa-Cre::Ai32 mice. Pulse times and laps are in two sessions only, so the light responses during ripples, theta and place fields are tested on those two; the ripple modulation of firing is tested on all sessions. The intracellular recordings and the light intensity levels are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Valero et al. (2022) from dandiset 000568

outcomes.statement: CA1 pyramidal neurons were recorded and probed in four CaMKIIa-Cre::Ai32 mice, 822 pyramidal neurons in all, 43.3 plus or minus 8.37 per session.
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), all 28 sessions, 4 mice and 48.2 putative pyramidal cells per session (SD 12.18) match, but the total is 1351 against 822. Under reading (b), the 22 sessions naming the uLED protocol, 3 mice, 1047 cells and 47.6 per session. 822 cells at 43.3 per session would be about 19 sessions. With thresholds of 2.5 and 10 Hz the total is 1205 or 1441.
deviations: Pyramidal cells are units with a baseline rate below 5 Hz, as the files carry no cell type; the paper classified cells by other features.
The paper does not say which sessions it used; two readings are shown.

outcomes.statement: uLEDs were driven with 20 ms pulses at random sites with randomly variable 20 to 40 ms offsets, so that the stimulation of each site recurred at about 0.3 to 0.6 s intervals.
outcomes.notes: Pulses last 19.87 ms (sess9) and 19.63 ms (sess12). The median interval between pulses of one uLED is 0.281 to 0.383 s for the four uLEDs with at least 1000 pulses, within 0.27 to 0.66 s. The median offset from the end of one pulse to the start of the next is 60.4 and 80.0 ms, outside 18 to 44 ms; 31.8% and 30.2% of offsets fall within 20 to 40 ms, and the 95th percentiles are 241 and 328 ms. Most pulses are not in the files (5.76 and 7.50 deposited pulses per s in PreStim against about 17 to 25 implied by the protocol; in sess9 the offsets fall only near multiples of 20 ms), so the longer offsets span missing pulses and the protocol's offsets cannot be measured from the files.
deviations: Two sessions of 28, the only ones with pulse times.
The files hold only part of the pulses, so the offsets between pulses are measured on the deposited ones.

outcomes.statement: Of 822 pyramidal neurons, 611 responded to light from the uLEDs.
outcomes.notes: Under reading (b), all stimulation epochs, 66 of 91 putative pyramidal cells (72.5%, 95% interval 62.2 to 81.4%) respond to at least one uLED. Under reading (a), the PreStim epoch, 57 of 91 (62.6%, 51.9 to 72.6%), outside tolerance. Of 364 unit and uLED tests in PreStim, 68 pass all three parts of the test; on sham onsets (jittered by up to 200 ms, or moved into BaselinePre) none of 364 passes. For reading (b), with the onsets of all stimulation epochs jittered by up to 200 ms, none of 364 tests passes either. No putative pyramidal cell on shank Group3 responds (0 of 17), and that shank's uLEDs are likely among those whose pulses are not in the files. Without Group3, 57 of 74 (77.0%) under (a), within tolerance, and 66 of 74 (89.2%) under (b), above it. The criterion lists (a) first but only (b) matches, so the measured value is that of (b).
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse (91 putative pyramidal cells), not 822 cells.

The response test is the one in the first author's later code (HippoCookBook getuLEDResponse.m), with 500 bootstrap sets drawn on a 1 ms grid and shared across units, and a minimum of 1000 pulses per uLED in place of 2000; the paper's own test is in its unavailable Methods.
Which pulses the paper tested is not stated; two readings are shown and the claim matches under reading (b) only.
Cells near uLEDs whose pulses are not in the files cannot be tested for a response to them.

outcomes.statement: Light-induced spike responses of individual pyramidal cells decreased during sharp-wave ripples (n = 485 neurons, P < 1e-55, Wilcoxon paired signed-rank test).
outcomes.source: Results, third paragraph; Figure 1, F to I
outcomes.notes: In 57 light-responsive putative pyramidal cells, light minus control rate is 0.30 Hz (median) in windows overlapping ripples and 2.68 Hz outside, lower inside in 49 of 57 (Wilcoxon p = 6.8e-09), and in each session (p = 7.8e-06 and 9.5e-07). As a ratio, 1.25 inside and 2.89 outside (53 of 56, p = 8.6e-10). The paper's n of 485 and P < 1e-55 cannot be reached with two sessions. The control windows, the 20 ms before each onset, are dark under the stated protocol, so the missing pulses do not enter them.
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse.
Ripples are the deposited ripple intervals; a window counts as inside a ripple when it overlaps one.
Control windows are the 20 ms before each pulse with no uLED on.

outcomes.statement: The firing-rate change of pyramidal neurons during SPW-Rs is negatively correlated with their baseline firing rate (rho = -0.19, P < 1e-7).
outcomes.notes: Over 1166 putative pyramidal cells of 24 sessions, the log2 ratio of the rate inside ripples to outside is negatively correlated with the baseline rate (rho = -0.437, p = 1.8e-55). It is negative in every subject (-0.37 to -0.71) and every session, and significant in all sessions but three (fCamk1 sess13 p = 0.12, fCamk3 sess13 p = 0.29, fCamk5 sess14 p = 0.81). This is stronger than -0.19 and outside the tolerance of 0.068. The difference reading gives rho = -0.002 (p = 0.95). Without the two sessions in the analysis whose ripples fail the clock check (the third has under 50 first-epoch ripples), n = 1055 and rho = -0.468; in the 22 sessions whose first epoch is labelled BaselinePre, -0.450; against the rate outside ripples, -0.466.
deviations: The paper's measure of rate change is in the unavailable supplement; two readings were fixed before the analysis and they disagree.
The tolerance is the sampling half-width at n = 822, not 10% of the value.

outcomes.statement: During track running, the light-induced rate gain is largest at the trough of the theta cycle (P < 1e-6, Wilcoxon test).
outcomes.source: Results, fourth paragraph; Figure 2, A and B
outcomes.notes: In 57 light-responsive putative pyramidal cells during laps, the gain is 2.04 Hz in the trough half of theta and 2.07 Hz in the peak half (medians), higher at the trough in 22 of 57 cells (Wilcoxon p = 0.14) and significant in neither session. In 60-degree bins the gain is largest 30 degrees after the peak (2.13 Hz). The stored LFP rate is 1250 Hz from 0 s and the LFP ends with the last epoch; ripple-band power at 44 and 27 deposited ripple peaks inside the Maze epoch is 113 and 78 times its mean; spikes of putative pyramidal cells in control windows have a circular mean phase of 128 and 130 degrees, in the trough half; the theta-band LFP averaged around onsets deviates by at most 27.1 and 8.5 against a theta-band SD of 406 and 770.
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse.
The LFP channel (largest ripple power), the theta band (6 to 10 Hz) and the half-cycle split are choices made here; the paper's are in its unavailable Methods.

outcomes.statement: More than half of the pyramidal neurons were place cells, 73% of light-responsive and 71% of non-responsive neurons, with no difference between them (P = 0.90, chi-squared test).
outcomes.notes: 48 of 57 light-responsive (84.2%, 95% interval 72.1 to 92.5%) and 24 of 34 non-responsive (70.6%, 52.5 to 84.9%) putative pyramidal cells are place cells; the paper's chi-squared test finds no difference (p = 0.20), as in the paper. The non-responsive fraction is within tolerance, the responsive one above it. Per session 83% against 56% (sess9) and 86% against 83% (sess12). Over all putative pyramidal cells 79.1% are place cells. With all time without a deposited pulse as control time and the earlier field rule (the round-1 analysis) the fractions are 78.9% and 52.9% with p = 0.018; the control time alone changes 5 cells, the field rule alone 1, both 11. Some non-responsive cells may respond to uLEDs whose pulses are not in the files.
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse.

Place fields follow a port of buzcode's bz_findPlaceFields1D with its defaults, on control maps from the windows dark under the stated protocol (the 20 ms before each deposited onset and after each offset), since most pulses are not in the files; the paper's standard definition is in its unavailable Methods. The files do not follow the protocol exactly (3.2% and 3.8% of deposited offsets in PreStim are under 20 ms), so missing pulses may fall in some of these windows.

outcomes.statement: The light-induced rate increase is higher within than outside the place field (n = 553 place fields, P < 1e-115, Wilcoxon test).
outcomes.source: Results, fourth paragraph; Figure 2, C to E
outcomes.notes: Over 80 control place fields of 48 light-responsive putative pyramidal cells, gain is 3.95 Hz in the field and 1.37 Hz outside (medians), higher in the field for 61 of 80 (Wilcoxon p = 1e-08) and in each session (p = 9.5e-07 and 0.0018). As a ratio of light to control the in-field value is lower (2.19 against 2.77, p = 4.3e-05), so the increase is larger in hertz but not relative to the control rate.
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse; 80 fields against 553.
Control rates come from the windows dark under the stated protocol.

outcomes.statement: The in-field gain is positively correlated with the out-of-field firing rate (rho = 0.17, P < 1e-5) and with the home-cage firing rate of the neuron (rho = 0.25, P < 1e-7).
outcomes.notes: Over 80 fields, rho is -0.018 (p = 0.87) for the out-of-field rate and -0.063 (p = 0.58) for the home-cage rate, both outside tolerance. With one field per cell, rho is 0.131 for the out-of-field rate (within tolerance) and -0.003 for the home-cage rate.
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse; 80 fields against 553.

outcomes.statement: Light responses in the home cage before the track were stronger in place cells than in non-place cells (P < 1e-4, Kruskal-Wallis test).
outcomes.notes: The PreStim light response (best uLED) has a median of 1.90 Hz in 72 place cells and 1.03 Hz in 19 non-place cells, higher in place cells but not significantly (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.19; z-scored p = 0.25). It is significant in sess9 (p = 0.027) and not in sess12 (0.94 against 1.19 Hz, p = 0.85). Within halves of the baseline rate neither difference is significant (p = 0.6 and 0.2).
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse; 19 non-place cells.
Place cells as in figs11-place-cell-fraction.

outcomes.statement: Optogenetic depolarization revealed place fields in the majority of non-place cells, 289 of 417 (69.3%).
outcomes.source: Results, fifth paragraph; Figure 3, B and C
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), 7 of 9 light-responsive non-place cells (77.8%, 95% interval 40.0 to 97.2%) have a light field, 1.6 points above the tolerance of 69.3 plus or minus 6.9; under reading (b), 6 of 19 non-place cells (31.6%, 12.6 to 56.6%), below it and above the 15.8% found in control maps thinned at random to the time of the light maps. Reading (a) rests on 9 cells and its interval includes the paper's value. Its light maps use only each cell's own uLEDs (2.6% to 6.2% of lap time); control maps thinned to that time give a field in 31.7% of draws on average over the 9 cells.
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse; 19 non-place cells against 417.
The paper's denominator and its rule for an induced field are in its unavailable Methods; two readings are shown.

outcomes.statement: The spatial location of light-induced spikes matches that of spikes without stimulation, both for place fields of place cells (P < 1e-40) and for unmasked place fields of non-place cells, whose sparse control spikes form ghost fields (P < 1e-10).
outcomes.source: Results, fifth paragraph; Figure 3, C and E
outcomes.notes: For 70 field directions of light-responsive place cells the light peak follows the control peak (Pearson r = 0.806, p = 3.9e-17). For 14 light field directions of 7 non-place cells r = 0.321 (p = 0.26). In the shuffle variant, 35.7% of unmasked peaks lie within 4.4 cm of the control peak against 14.6% for shuffled pairings (p = 0.014), which is closer to the paper's test against shuffles. 8 of the 14 unmasked field directions come from sess9.
deviations: Pearson correlation of peak positions in place of the paper's chi-squared test against 500 shuffles, whose details are in the unavailable Methods; a shuffle test is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Place fields during light stimulation were more stable between the first and second halves of the session than during control epochs, for both true place fields and unmasked place fields (P < 1e-9 and P < 1e-19, two-way ANOVA).
outcomes.notes: Light maps are not more stable than control maps between laps 11-60 and 71-120 (place fields 0.664 against 0.714, light higher in 28 of 70, p = 0.058; unmasked fields 0.187 against 0.527, 6 of 14, p = 0.39). Against control maps from as many 20 ms control windows as light windows, place fields 0.664 against 0.602 (p = 0.68) and unmasked fields 0.187 against 0.293 (p = 0.67). Control maps from stimulated laps only give the same medians (p = 0.059 and 0.39), as they must, since dark windows lie only next to deposited pulses. The two-way ANOVA finds an effect of condition (p = 0.046), with light the less stable by the medians.
deviations: Control maps use the windows dark under the stated protocol (19% to 20% of lap time); the paper's control epochs were random 20 ms intervals between pulses, shown as a time-matched variant.
Wilcoxon tests in place of the paper's two-way ANOVA, which is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Spatial information of control and light-stimulated epochs is correlated, and the light-boosted increase is stronger for unmasked place fields of non-place cells than for place cells (P < 1e-15, Kruskal-Wallis test).
outcomes.notes: Control and light spatial information are correlated for place fields (rho = 0.655, p = 7.6e-10) and for unmasked fields (rho = 0.574, p = 0.032). The increase is larger for unmasked fields (median 0.03 against -0.03 bits/spike, Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.039), far from the paper's P < 1e-15. Against time-matched control maps both correlations hold (place rho = 0.501, p = 1e-05; unmasked rho = 0.609, p = 0.021), but the increase is negative in both groups (place -0.10, unmasked -0.17) and does not differ (p = 0.3); as a ratio it does not differ either (p = 0.14). The paper's control epochs are random 20 ms intervals between the light pulses, which the time-matched variant follows most closely, and the dark-window control maps are themselves a revision of the criterion's control (all time with no uLED on). Part 1 holds and part 2 does not. Unmasked fields are chosen for a light field and no control field, which favours a larger increase by construction; the paper defines its groups the same way. Changed from reproduced after verification round 3 agreed.
deviations: Control maps use the windows dark under the stated protocol; time-matched control windows are a variant, under which the larger increase in unmasked fields does not hold.

outcomes.statement: Cofiring of place cell pairs during SPW-Rs in the home cage is positively correlated with their spatial overlap on the track (P < 1e-27), while pairs of a place cell and a non-place cell show no such relationship (P = 0.11).
outcomes.source: Results, sixth paragraph; Figure 4, B and C
outcomes.notes: Over 1264 place cell pairs, ripple cofiring is correlated with spatial overlap (rho = 0.060, p = 0.032), so part 1 holds, weakly and in sess9 only (0.119, p = 0.0015; sess12 0.019, p = 0.66). Over 698 place and non-place pairs the paper's test finds no correlation (rho = 0.062, p = 0.1), so part 2 holds, but the coefficient is as large as for place cell pairs. Correlation of participation per ripple gives 0.054 (p = 0.056) and 0.072 (p = 0.058).
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse.
Cofiring as the Pearson correlation of spike counts per deposited ripple, a choice made here; the paper's measure is in its unavailable Methods.

outcomes.statement: With light-induced spikes, the relationship between SPW-R cofiring and spatial overlap appears for pairs that include non-place cells (P < 1e-5, Spearman correlation).
outcomes.source: Results, sixth paragraph; Figure 4, C and D (legend panel D)
outcomes.notes: Over 231 pairs of light-responsive place and non-place cells, cofiring is not significantly correlated with the overlap of light maps (rho = 0.075, p = 0.25; sess9 0.108, p = 0.16; sess12 -0.062, p = 0.65). With control maps the same pairs give rho = 0.110 (p = 0.094).
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse.

outcomes.statement: Stronger light (three intensities) decreased the light-induced response during SPW-Rs, increased the in-field gain of place cells several-fold, and increased the in-field gain of unmasked fields (Figure 1J, Figure 2F, Figure 3D; Friedman tests).
outcomes.notes: The pulse series hold one value per uLED in each of the two sessions with pulses (19 in sess9, 62623 to 63599 in sess12, stated as watts), so no pulse has an intensity level, and the other 26 sessions have no pulse series. The paper's other named data location, the Buzsaki Lab Databank, serves data through Globus with an account and no pinned identifier.

outcomes.statement: Intracellular recordings in which the membrane potential was varied reproduce the decreased gain during SPW-Rs (five cells in anesthetized rats and five in head-fixed mice, P = 0.002).
outcomes.source: Results, third paragraph; Figure 1, K to M
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds extracellular recordings of four mice only; the intracellular recordings in rats and head-fixed mice are not in it. The lab's data page lists this dandiset for the paper and otherwise points to a Globus endpoint without a pinned identifier.

outcomes.statement: During SPW-Rs, excitatory neurons increased their firing rates more than inhibitory neurons.
outcomes.notes: The units carry no cell type, and the no-raw-data files hold no waveforms. A rate threshold separates cells by the very quantity the claim compares, so it was not used for this claim. Waveforms could be taken from the raw signal, but the full files are 17 to 54 GB each and six of them have no raw signal. As a proxy shown in the notebook, units at or above 5 Hz raise their rate inside ripples less than putative pyramidal cells (median log2 ratio 0.75 against 1.19, p = 0.00065); since the ripple gain falls with baseline rate within putative pyramidal cells alone (figs10), this split would show the same without interneurons, so it does not test the claim.

outcomes.statement: Decoding of position is most accurate from light-boosted spikes of place cells, and light-induced spikes of non-place cells predict position better than control spikes of place cells (P = 0.001, Tukey test).
outcomes.notes: The decoder, its spatial bins, time windows and cross-validation are described in the supplement, which could not be obtained; the main text and legend do not fix them. The data for it (two sessions with laps and pulses) are in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: ICA assemblies of place cells in the home cage show higher spatial correlation than chance, mixed assemblies of place and non-place cells do not, and with unmasked place fields they reach the level of place-cell assemblies.
outcomes.source: Results, sixth paragraph; Figure 4, E and F
outcomes.notes: The ICA assembly detection (bin size, significance of components) and the chance level for spatial correlation are in the unavailable supplement. The legend gives only the member threshold of 2 SD. The data are in the dandiset for two sessions.

outcomes.statement: Sequential firing of place cells is correlated with spike sequences during SPW-Rs, and the fraction of SPW-Rs with significant trajectories increases when unmasked place fields are included in the template (P < 1e-4, Friedman test).
outcomes.source: Results, sixth paragraph; Figure 4, G and H
outcomes.notes: The Bayesian decoding of ripples, the template construction and the shuffle are in the unavailable supplement; the legend gives only 500 shuffles. The data are in the dandiset for two sessions.

findings.statement: Light pulse times are deposited for 2 of 28 sessions (fCamk1 sess9 and sess12). Twenty other sessions name uLED stimulation in their epochs but hold no pulse series, so their light responses cannot be computed. Laps are also in these two sessions only.

The OptogeneticSeries are stated in watts but hold one value per uLED, 19 in sess9 and 62623 to 63599 in sess12, not a light power (the paper gives 0.02 to 0.1 uW). No light intensity per pulse is stored, so the paper's three intensities cannot be recovered.

The files hold pulse series for 6 of the probe's 12 uLEDs (Site3 to Site8), two of them with only 120 to 221 pulses, and most pulses of the protocol are missing. In PreStim the deposited pulses come at 5.76 and 7.50 per s, where the stated protocol implies about 17 to 25; in fCamk1 sess9 the offsets between deposited pulses fall only near multiples of 20 ms, the gaps left by missing pulses. No putative pyramidal cell on shank Group3 responds to any deposited uLED. Time without a deposited pulse therefore cannot be taken as dark.

Every session is deposited twice, as a full file and a no-raw-data file; in all 28 sessions the two hold the same units, spike times, ripples and position. The full file of fCamk3 sess20 is named sub-fCamk3_behavior+ecephys+image.nwb, without its session.
The full file of fCamk3 sess17 is 28 MB and holds 378 s of raw signal and 6850 s of LFP of a 34621 s session. The six full files of fCamk1 sess13 to sess19 hold the LFP but no raw signal.
Units carry no cell type and the no-raw-data files no waveforms, so pyramidal cells and interneurons cannot be told apart as in the paper.
session_start_time is 2016-03-15 in every file, while the session ids date the recordings to 2020 and 2021.
The linearized position holds values from 0 to 110 cm (the track length) but has a conversion factor of 100, which would put it at 0 to 110 m.

Six sessions (fCamk2 sess1 to sess4, fCamk3 sess13, fCamk5 sess10) name their epochs only by a time stamp, without behavioral paradigm or manipulation. fCamk2 sessions have no position and 0 to 1110 ripples.

The dandiset holds 28 sessions and 1351 units with a baseline rate below 5 Hz, where the paper reports 822 pyramidal neurons at 43.3 per session (about 19 sessions). It does not say which sessions the paper used. 14 sessions include CNO or DMSO epochs, which the paper does not describe.

In fCamk3 sess13, fCamk3 sess17 and fCamk5 sess10 the deposited ripple intervals mark population bursts weakly (population rate 1.2 to 1.98 times that 1 s later, against at least twice in the other 22 sessions with ripples). fCamk5 sess10 has 217 events with a median length of 109 ms.

The paper gives randomly variable 20 to 40 ms offsets between pulses, the files' description 40 to 60 ms. Measured onset to onset, 30% to 32% of the deposited intervals fall in 40 to 60 ms; measured end to start, 30% to 32% fall in 20 to 40 ms, and most others span missing pulses.

The paper's Materials and Methods are in its supplement. This attempt could not obtain the supplement from PMC or the publisher, and the analysis code the paper names (buzcode) is a general toolbox without scripts for its figures.

The paper reports 822 pyramidal neurons of which 73% of light-responsive and 71% of non-responsive neurons were place cells, which leaves about 230 non-place cells, but gives the unmasked fraction as 289 of 417 non-place cells.
The units table of some files lacks the shank column (group_id); columns are spike_times, unit_name, clu_id and, in the others, group_id.
