attempts.paper_title: State-dependent modulation of spiny projection neurons controls levodopa-induced dyskinesia in a mouse model of Parkinson’s disease
attempts.entry_title: State-dependent modulation of spiny projection neurons in levodopa-induced dyskinesia (Zhai et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Zhai, Cui, Wokosin, Sun, Tkatch, Crittenden, Graybiel and Surmeier (2025) on dandiset 001538. It measures somatic excitability (rheobase and spike counts) and the dendritic excitability index of dSPNs and iSPNs in the LID off- and on-states and under D1R, D2R and M1R antagonists, CDGI deletion and M1R deletion, and evoked ACh release with GRAB-ACh3.0. It links the recordings to the paper's per-cell tables on Zenodo. The Sr2+-oEPSC, ACh and AIM data hold too few cells or mice for most of the paper's tests, and the spine data are raw stacks only.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Zhai et al. (2025) from dandiset 001538

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's somatic current-step recordings are those behind the paper's somatic excitability figures, and the spike counts computed from them agree with the paper's per-cell tables.
outcomes.source: Figures 1E, 3C, 6C, 7C and 9D; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: Groups are matched by name and every group the dandiset holds has the paper's n (12 of 12 groups, 123 cells). 90 of 123 cells (73.2%) match a row of the paper's table exactly over 20 to 300 pA and 105 (85.4%) within 3 spikes, below the 80% and 95% of the criterion; 108 have the same rheobase as their best match. dSPN on has the fewest exact matches (6 of 15). The best matches are not one-to-one (9 paper rows are the best match of two or three cells); with each row used once, 89 cells (72.4%) match exactly and 103 (83.7%) within 3 spikes. The best-match rows follow the dandiset's order by date and cell number, every cell at its own rank in 8 of 12 groups and 10 of 15, 11 of 15, 11 of 12 and 10 of 11 cells in the others. Of the 14 cells with a repeated step, keeping the last sweep in place of the first gives the same best-match difference in 13 and a closer one in 1.
deviations: The paper's spike counts come from its script run on Prairie View exports; the differences of 1 to 24 spikes may come from the export or from cells whose steps are missing or repeated in the files (18 cells miss a step, 14 repeat one).

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's dendritic line scans are those behind the paper's dendritic excitability index figures, and the index computed from them agrees with the paper's per-cell values.
outcomes.source: Figures 1I, 3F, 6D and 7F; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: Three site series hold six trials, two sites under one name; split, they give their cells 0.293, 0.146 and 0.327 against the paper's 0.299, 0.146 and 0.309. With the split, 91 of 92 cells have an index (iSPN on+sul 20190508 cell 3 has only a distal site). Counts of cells with an index equal the paper's n in 9 of 10 groups, and counts of cells with dendritic sites in 10 of 10, so every group is matched, by order or (Figure 6D) by date and letter. Over 91 matched cells the index differs from the paper's by a median of 2.9% (78 within 10%, Spearman 0.938). Two cells differ by more than the paper's value, dSPN on+SCH 20190411 cell 1 (0.584 against 0.228; only its second pair of sites is in the dandiset) and iSPN off 20160524 cell 2 (1.062 against 0.527; its first proximal site has one trial, and without it the cell gives 0.553). The best-match rows of the somatic link follow the dandiset's order (link-somatic-cells), which supports matching by order. With the sites as labelled, 89 of 92 cells have an index.
deviations: Outside Figure 6D the paper's table has no cell identifiers, so cells are matched by order, an assumption supported by the somatic link.
The background constants of the paper's script (55 red, 161 green) are used for every session, as the files carry no per-session background.
Three six-trial series are split into their first and last three trials, the half with the smaller area taken as distal, a choice made here from the data; the sites as labelled are a variant.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's Sr2+-oEPSC recordings are cells of the paper's Figures 2 and 4, and their events agree with the paper's per-cell values.
outcomes.source: Figures 2G to 2I and 4F to 4H; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: All 14 dandiset cells match a paper identifier (date and session letter); the paper has 33 cells (17 off, 16 on), so the dandiset holds one cell per mouse. In every cell the detector here finds fewer events (2 to 85, against 29 to 127 in the paper's tables) and a higher mean amplitude than the paper's events; 2 of 14 cells are within 25% on both, and also 2 of 14 when the paper's amplitude is read as its per-cell value (0.70 to 0.96 times the mean of its histogram events). In 20230405b (2 events against 73) the detection window opens on the slow decay of a large synchronous current, and the small events on it stay below the threshold (figure in the notebook). The paper's frequency equals its event count over 3.6 s. With the paper's per-cell amplitudes, on-state dSPNs are all above off-state ones and on-state iSPNs all below (Mann-Whitney P = 0.057 each).
deviations: Events are found with a threshold detector written here (low-pass 1 kHz, five robust SD, local baseline); the paper used TaroTools with visual verification, which cannot be repeated.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's GRAB-ACh recordings are regions of the paper's Figure 5F, and the normalised areas computed from them agree with the paper's per-region values.
outcomes.source: Figure 5F; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds one region per mouse, 11 of the paper's 34 (3 of 13 unlesioned, 3 of 10 6-OHDA, 5 of 11 off-state). The paper's regions have no identifier linking them to mice; by the nearest vector of single-pulse areas only 5 of 11 mice have a paper region within 0.05 on every treatment (the 20240402 mouse within 0.007), so the regions cannot be identified. One paper region is the best match of two off-state mice; with each region used once, 5 of 11 are still within 0.05.
deviations: The stimulus time is taken from the trial table (3 s after the trial start in six files), where the paper's script fixes 10 s.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's AIM score tables are mice of the paper's Figures 8 and 10, with genotypes and scores that agree with the paper's tables.
outcomes.source: Figures 8B, 8C and 10B; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: 7 of 9 dandiset mice are in the paper's tables (4124 and 5871 are not). The two Figure 10 mice (5844 control, 5846 M1R deletion) have totals equal to the paper's in all 10 sessions; the five Figure 8 mice (1945, 2519, 2828 and 6572 KO, 2587 wild type) agree in 5 of 25 sessions (for 1945, session 1, 33.5 against 27.0). The dandiset's own genotype labels for the CDGI mice contradict each other, so the paper's labels were used. The paper's tables give session totals only; for the Figure 8 mice they equal neither the dandiset's sums over 20 to 80 min nor, outside those 5 sessions, the sums over all time points (1945 session 1 has four time points summing to 33.5), so the scores differ, not only the time points summed.
deviations: The paper's session total is taken to be the sum over the session's time points; the Figure 8 mice have 4 time points in some dandiset sessions and 6 in others.

outcomes.statement: In dSPNs the rheobase is lower in the LID on-state than in the off-state.
outcomes.notes: Rheobase on-state 140 pA against off-state 220 pA (15 cells each from 10 and 8 mice), Mann-Whitney P = 8.86e-06, effect r = -0.95. With one value per mouse P = 0.000425 and complete separation.

outcomes.statement: In on-state dSPNs suprathreshold current steps evoke more spikes than in off-state dSPNs across a range of intensities.
outcomes.notes: Summed spikes 20 to 300 pA, median 88 on against 36 off, P = 8.8e-05 (0.00015 for the 22 cells with every step). The on-state median is higher at every step from 120 to 300 pA (per-step P at most 0.012).
deviations: The paper shows F-I curves without a test; the summed count and its test were chosen here.

outcomes.statement: Bath application of the D1R antagonist SCH 23390 does not reverse the lower rheobase of on-state dSPNs.
outcomes.notes: Rheobase on-state 140 pA (15 cells) against on-state with SCH 140 pA (10 cells), P = 1.0, effect r = 0.007. In the 5 cells recorded in both conditions the median paired difference is 0 pA (Wilcoxon P = 1.0). Five cells are in both groups, so the unpaired test's samples are not independent; the criterion follows the paper's test.

outcomes.statement: The dendritic excitability index of dSPNs is higher in the on-state than in the off-state.
outcomes.notes: Index on-state 0.476 against off-state 0.330 (10 cells each), P = 0.0058 (exact 0.0039), effect r = 0.74; without background P = 0.0046; with a basal-ratio rule of 0.8 to 1.25 (8 cells each) P = 0.0070; with the sites as labelled P = 0.0091.
deviations: Background constants from the paper's script; basal-ratio rule (0.5 to 2) chosen here, dropping no pair; one six-trial series split into two sites.

outcomes.statement: SCH 23390 reverses the higher dendritic excitability of on-state dSPNs.
outcomes.notes: The criterion (P < 0.05 with the SCH median lower) is not met, though the difference has the stated direction. On-state with SCH 0.419 (9 cells) against on-state 0.476 (10 cells), P = 0.0662 (exact 0.0653), effect r = -0.51; with the stricter basal-ratio rule P = 0.524. The difference from the paper comes from one cell, SCH 20190411 cell 1, whose index is 0.584 here and 0.228 in the paper's table; the dandiset holds only its second pair of sites. Without that cell P = 0.0266; with the paper's value for it P = 0.016 (exact 0.0133, the paper's P). The other eight SCH cells differ from the paper's values by 2.4% to 10.9%. That the missing sites explain the difference is an inference from the recovered P, as the paper does not list each cell's sites.
deviations: Matching the SCH cells to the paper's rows by order is an assumption (link-dendritic-cells).

outcomes.statement: The amplitude of Sr2+-oEPSCs evoked from cortical afferents is larger in on-state than in off-state dSPNs.
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds one cell per mouse, 3 off-state and 4 on-state dSPNs of the paper's 10 and 8. With 3 against 4 cells the smallest attainable two-sided Mann-Whitney P is 0.057, so the paper's test cannot reach P < 0.05. The per-cell values are shown under link-sr-cells; with the detector here the on-state amplitudes are all above the off-state ones (P = 0.057).

outcomes.statement: The frequency of Sr2+-oEPSCs in dSPNs does not differ between states.
outcomes.notes: Same 3 against 4 cells as fig2h; the test cannot detect a difference at P < 0.05 whatever the data, so the claim of absence cannot be judged. The frequencies are shown under link-sr-cells (P = 0.229).

outcomes.statement: dSPN spine density falls in the off-state, and mushroom spines are more common in the on-state than in the off-state.
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds the two-photon z-stacks of dSPN dendrites (off- and on-state) but no spine counts; none of the 86 spine files has a processing module or analysis entry. The paper deconvolved them in AutoQuant X3 and counted spines semi-automatically in NeuronStudio with manual classification of mushroom spines, a procedure that cannot be repeated from its description (also not runnable here, AutoQuant being commercial software). No control or 6-OHDA stacks for dSPNs were found. The per-cell densities are in the paper's Zenodo tables.

outcomes.statement: In iSPNs the rheobase is higher in the on-state than in the off-state.
outcomes.notes: Rheobase on-state 160 pA (11 cells, 8 mice) against off-state 120 pA (12 cells, 5 mice), P = 0.000829, effect r = 0.81; one value per mouse P = 0.00899.

outcomes.statement: The F-I relationship of iSPNs shifts to the right in the on-state.
outcomes.notes: Summed spikes 65 on against 118.5 off, P = 7.2e-05 (0.000165 for complete cells); lower on-state median at every step from 120 to 300 pA (per-step P at most 0.012).
deviations: The summed count and its test were chosen here.

outcomes.statement: Sulpiride does not alter the somatic excitability of on-state iSPNs.
outcomes.notes: Rheobase on-state 160 pA (11) against on-state with sulpiride 120 pA (7), P = 0.143, effect r = -0.43. The two cells recorded in both conditions have a lower rheobase with sulpiride (160 to 120 and 160 to 100 pA), so the absence rests on the test's power. Those two cells are in both groups, so the unpaired samples are not independent; the criterion follows the paper's test.

outcomes.statement: The dendritic excitability index of iSPNs falls in the on-state compared with the off-state.
outcomes.notes: Index on-state 0.339 (10) against off-state 0.524 (10), P = 0.0073 (exact 0.0052), effect r = -0.72; without background P = 0.0073; with the sites as labelled (9 on-state cells) P = 0.0128; dropping sites with fewer than 3 trials P = 0.0091. With the stricter basal-ratio rule (0.8 to 1.25, 9 cells each) P = 0.0774, so the result depends on keeping pairs whose basal ratios differ by more than 25%. The stricter rule moves fig3f-ispn-dendritic-sul-no-change the other way (P = 0.0663, which would meet that criterion).
deviations: One on-state cell gets its index only from splitting a six-trial series into two sites.
The Methods keep pairs with similar G0/R0 without a threshold; the 0.5 to 2 rule chosen here drops no pair.

outcomes.statement: Sulpiride does not significantly alter dendritic excitability in on-state iSPNs.
outcomes.notes: The paper's test finds the difference the claim says is absent. On-state with sulpiride 0.506 (7 cells) against on-state 0.339 (10 cells), P = 0.0097, effect r = 0.74; the paper reports P = 0.0545 with 8 and 10 cells, and its own medians go the same way (0.499 and 0.345). With the sites as labelled P = 0.0164, with the stricter basal-ratio rule P = 0.0663. The sulpiride cell without an index (20190508 cell 3, only a distal site in the dandiset) has 0.217 in the paper's table; with that value P = 0.0545, the paper's P. Under the main basal-ratio rule the outcome turns on that one cell; under the stricter rule P = 0.0663 without it, which would also meet the criterion, so the outcome depends on the basal-ratio rule as well. That the missing site explains the difference is an inference from the recovered P, as the paper does not list each cell's sites.
deviations: One sulpiride cell has no index here (only a distal site).

outcomes.statement: The amplitude of Sr2+-oEPSCs is smaller in on-state than in off-state iSPNs.
outcomes.notes: One cell per mouse, 3 off-state and 4 on-state iSPNs of the paper's 7 and 8; the smallest attainable P is 0.057. With the detector here the on-state amplitudes are not all below the off-state ones (P = 0.229), while the paper's own per-cell values for these cells are (P = 0.057); shown under link-sr-cells.

outcomes.statement: The frequency of Sr2+-oEPSCs in iSPNs does not differ between states.
outcomes.notes: Same 3 against 4 cells as fig4g; the claim of absence cannot be judged by a test that cannot reach P < 0.05.

outcomes.statement: Apparent iSPN spine density (2PLSM) falls after the lesion, returns in the off-state and falls in the on-state, in total and mushroom spines.
outcomes.notes: Two-photon z-stacks of iSPN dendrites are in the dandiset (off- and on-state, CDGI KO, M1R antagonist, M1R deletion) but no counts; counting needs AutoQuant deconvolution and semi-automatic NeuronStudio reconstruction with manual checks, which the paper does not describe well enough to repeat. The control and 6-OHDA stacks the lesion part needs are not in the dandiset (data_missing); the off- and on-state part is blocked by the counting alone.

outcomes.statement: Confocal spine density of iSPN proximal dendrites is higher than the 2PLSM estimate (median 2.084 against 1.243 spines per um), falls after the lesion, rises modestly in the off-state and falls in the on-state.
outcomes.notes: Eleven confocal files of sparsely labelled iSPN dendrites (3 control, 3 6-OHDA, 3 off and 2 on) are in the dandiset, of the paper's 87 dendrites, with no counts. Counting used Imaris 10 with trained pixel classification and manual correction, which cannot be repeated from its description (and Imaris is commercial software).

outcomes.statement: Evoked ACh release (GRAB-ACh3.0) in slices from LID off-state mice is greater than in unlesioned striatum.
outcomes.notes: Single-pulse normalised area without drug, off-state 0.359 (5 mice) against unlesioned 0.112 (3 mice), P = 0.0357, the smallest attainable (complete separation). Burst stimulation gives the same; the unnormalised dF/F0 area does not (P = 0.25).
deviations: One region per mouse, 8 of the paper's 24 regions in these two groups.
Stimulus time from the trial table.

outcomes.statement: Evoked ACh release in the off-state is similar to that after a 6-OHDA lesion.
outcomes.notes: 6-OHDA 0.240 (3 mice) against off-state 0.359 (5 mice), P = 0.143, effect r = 0.73; burst P = 1.0. With 3 and 5 mice the test detects only complete separation, so the absence is weakly supported.
deviations: One region per mouse, 8 of the paper's 21 regions in these two groups.
The test cannot find any difference short of complete separation, so this claim of absence passes with little power.

outcomes.statement: Evoked ACh release is markedly elevated in 6-OHDA-lesioned striatum compared with unlesioned striatum.
outcomes.notes: 3 unlesioned and 3 6-OHDA mice, one region each; the smallest attainable P for 3 against 3 is 0.10. The values (unlesioned 0.089 to 0.113, 6-OHDA 0.179 to 0.269) are shown under link-grab-rois.

outcomes.statement: In unlesioned striatum sulpiride increases and quinpirole suppresses evoked ACh release.
outcomes.notes: 3 unlesioned mice; a paired Wilcoxon test on 3 pairs cannot reach P < 0.05 (smallest 0.25). In all three, quinpirole lowers and sulpiride raises the area (shown under link-grab-rois).

outcomes.statement: Dopamine (50 nM) strongly suppresses evoked ACh release in 6-OHDA-lesioned and off-state striatum, and sulpiride has no effect after the lesion.
outcomes.notes: 3 6-OHDA and 5 off-state mice; paired tests on 3 or 5 pairs cannot reach P < 0.05 (smallest 0.25 and 0.0625). Dopamine lowers the area in all 8 mice (shown under link-grab-rois); sulpiride after the lesion raises it in two of three.

outcomes.statement: M1R antagonism throughout the off-state does not have a strong impact on the elevated somatic excitability of off-state iSPNs.
outcomes.notes: Rheobase vehicle 120 pA (8) against antagonist 140 pA (10), P = 0.681, effect r = 0.125; summed spikes P = 0.45.
deviations: The paper gives no test; its default Mann-Whitney test on rheobase was used.

outcomes.statement: M1R antagonism prevents the off-state elevation of iSPN dendritic excitability.
outcomes.notes: Index vehicle 0.451 (9) against antagonist 0.269 (7), P = 0.0229, effect r = -0.68; with the stricter basal-ratio rule P = 0.0164.

outcomes.statement: M1R antagonism prevents the off-state elevation of apparent iSPN spine density.
outcomes.notes: Z-stacks are in the dandiset without counts (see fig4bc-ispn-spines).

outcomes.statement: Deletion of CDGI does not blunt the oscillation of iSPN somatic excitability between on- and off-states.
outcomes.notes: KO rheobase on-state 210 pA (8) against off-state 140 pA (13), P = 0.00104, effect r = 0.87; summed spikes P = 0.00335.
deviations: The paper shows F-I curves without a test; a Mann-Whitney test of rheobase was chosen here.

outcomes.statement: The off-state elevation of iSPN dendritic excitability is absent in CDGI KO mice (off against on not different), while it is present in wild type.
outcomes.notes: KO index off-state 0.312 (11) against on-state 0.286 (8), P = 0.310, effect r = -0.30 (P = 0.659 with the stricter rule, 0.315 with the sites as labelled); wild type P = 0.0073.
deviations: One KO off-state cell gets its index only from splitting a six-trial series into two sites.

outcomes.statement: The off-state increase in apparent iSPN spine density is absent in CDGI KO mice.
outcomes.notes: Z-stacks are in the dandiset without counts (see fig4bc-ispn-spines).

outcomes.statement: Axial, limb, orolingual and total AIMs are less severe in CDGI KO mice than in wild type.
outcomes.source: Figures 8B and 8C (repeated-measures two-way ANOVA, group P < 0.001 to 0.002)
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds AIM tables for 5 of the paper's 23 Figure 8 mice (4 KO, 1 wild type) and 2 mice not in the paper; with one wild-type mouse the paper's repeated-measures ANOVA cannot be run. The dandiset's genotype labels contradict each other, and the session totals of these mice differ from the paper's in 20 of 25 sessions (link-aim-mice, not reproduced).

outcomes.statement: Deletion of M1Rs from iSPNs does not alter the elevated somatic excitability of off-state iSPNs.
outcomes.notes: Rheobase control 160 pA (6) against M1R CRISPR 120 pA (8), P = 0.147, effect r = -0.48; summed spikes P = 0.245. The control group is 6 cells from 2 mice, so the absence rests on little power.
deviations: The paper gives no test; its default Mann-Whitney test on rheobase was used.

outcomes.statement: Deletion of M1Rs from iSPNs blunts the off-state increase in apparent spine density.
outcomes.notes: Z-stacks are in the dandiset without counts (see fig4bc-ispn-spines).

outcomes.statement: AIMs are attenuated by deletion of M1Rs in iSPNs.
outcomes.source: Figure 10B (repeated-measures two-way ANOVA, group P < 0.001 to 0.0015)
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds AIM tables for 2 of the paper's 21 Figure 10 mice, one control (5844) and one M1R deletion (5846), whose totals equal the paper's; one mouse per group cannot be tested. Mouse 5846 has lower totals than 5844 in every session.

outcomes.statement: dSPN somatic excitability (rheobase) rises after the 6-OHDA lesion and falls in the LID off-state.
outcomes.notes: On the paper's table, rheobase 120 pA after the lesion against 220 pA in controls (P = 0.000295) and 200 pA in the off-state against 120 pA (P = 9.54e-05). The paper reports P < 0.0001 for both.
deviations: Tested on the paper's per-cell table; the raw recordings in Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17260198 were not reanalysed.
outcomes.where: Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059 (per-cell rheobase, Figure 1F sheet); raw recordings in Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17260198

outcomes.statement: The dSPN dendritic excitability index is not changed by the 6-OHDA lesion or in the off-state.
outcomes.notes: On the paper's table, P = 0.82 and 0.903 (reported 0.824 and 0.905).
deviations: Tested on the paper's table, not the raw line scans.

outcomes.statement: iSPN somatic excitability is lowered by the 6-OHDA lesion and restored in the LID off-state.
outcomes.notes: On the paper's table, rheobase 200 pA after the lesion against 120 pA in controls (P = 0.000401) and 130 pA in the off-state (P = 0.000608); reported P = 0.002 for both.
deviations: Tested on the paper's table.

outcomes.statement: The iSPN dendritic excitability index rises after the lesion and stays raised in the off-state.
outcomes.notes: On the paper's table, 0.516 after the lesion and 0.519 off-state against 0.405 in controls (P = 0.0348 and 0.0242; reported 0.0327 and 0.0220).
deviations: Tested on the paper's table.

outcomes.statement: Oxotremorine-M increases bAP invasion of iSPN dendrites in wild-type but not in CDGI KO mice.
outcomes.notes: On the paper's table, wild type 8 of 10 increase, Wilcoxon P = 0.009766 (reported 0.0098); KO 4 of 12 increase, P = 0.4697 (reported 0.910). Pairs are formed by the table's experiment number (printed); an unpaired Mann-Whitney test gives 0.885 for KO and 0.0539 for wild type, so neither test gives the reported 0.910.
deviations: Tested on the paper's table; the oxo-M line scans are not in the dandiset.
outcomes.where: Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059 (Figure 7E sheet); raw line scans in Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17260198

outcomes.statement: Levodopa induces more contralateral rotations in CDGI KO mice than in wild type at the fifth dose.
outcomes.source: Figure 8A (P = 0.0092 in the text; the legend marks P < 0.05)
outcomes.notes: On the paper's table, KO 8.5 against wild type 4.25 rotations (10 and 12 mice), P = 0.012 (the text reports 0.0092, the legend P < 0.05).
deviations: Tested on the paper's table; the dandiset holds rotation videos for 7 CDGI-study mice without counts.

outcomes.statement: Levodopa induces more contralateral rotations in mice lacking M1Rs in iSPNs.
outcomes.notes: On the paper's table, 8.5 with M1R deletion against 6.0 in controls, P = 0.00782 (reported 0.0056).
deviations: Tested on the paper's table.

outcomes.statement: In MCI-Park mice, a low dose of levodopa increases locomotion profoundly only when M1Rs are deleted from the striatum; M1R deletion alone does not.
outcomes.notes: On the paper's tables, MCI-Park against control distance 4.678 against 10.35 m (P = 1.05e-05), time mobile P = 6.97e-06; M1R deletion alone P = 0.628 and 0.467; levodopa with deletion against levodopa alone 28.09 against 6.52 m (P = 0.000332) and 276.4 against 127.45 s (P = 0.000567).
deviations: Tested on the paper's tables; the open-field data are not in the dandiset.
outcomes.where: Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059 (Figure 10E and 10F sheets); raw ANY-maze data in Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17260198

findings.statement: The dandiset holds no patch-clamp recordings from unlesioned control or 6-OHDA-lesioned mice, which make up the control and 6-OHDA groups of Figures 1E, 1F, 1I, 3C, 3D and 3F (10, 12, 11 and 9 dSPNs; 21, 11, 14 and 9 iSPNs), nor the oxo-M line scans of Figure 7E or the open-field data of Figure 10. The paper's raw data on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.17260198) list folders for all of these.

The Sr2+-oEPSC files hold one cell per mouse (14 of the paper's 33 cells), the GRAB-ACh files one region per mouse (11 of 34 regions) and the AIM tables 7 of the paper's 44 mice plus two mice (4124, 5871) not in the paper. The dandiset does not say that it holds a subset or how the cells, regions and mice were chosen, and with these numbers the paper's tests cannot reach P < 0.05 for most comparisons.

Session names state a drug (D1RaSch, D2RaSul) for files that also hold baseline on-state sweeps. 11 cells in such files have a baseline condition; 7 of them were also recorded with the drug and 4 are baseline only (dSPN 20190507 cell 1, iSPN 20190408 cell 1, 20190409 cell 1 and 20190508 cell 2). The condition of each sweep is only in the RecordingsIndexTable column condition_subfolder; grouping by session name puts baseline cells in the drug groups.

The genotypes of the CDGI behaviour mice contradict each other. Subject genotype is Wild-type CDGI and every session name says WT for all of them; the AIM table's genotype column says CDGI Knockout, Wild Type or unknown, changing between sessions of one animal; the video files of mice 1945, 2519, 2587, 2828 and 6572 say CDGI KO. The paper lists 2587 as wild type and the others as KO.

The AIM session totals of the five Figure 8 mice in the dandiset differ from the paper's table in 20 of 25 sessions (mouse 1945 session 1, 33.5 against 27.0), while the two Figure 10 mice agree in all sessions. Some dandiset sessions have 4 time points and others 6.

Three dendritic site series hold six trials, two sites under one name, while the cell has no series of the other compartment with that number (iSPN 20160526 cell 3 Distal1, iSPN 20160608 cell 1 Proximal1, dSPN 20170204 cell 1 Proximal1); their first and last three trials differ in baseline and area. Split, they give the paper's values for these cells. One series holds a single trial (iSPN 20160524 cell 2 Proximal1), one two and one four.

Two dendritic cells lack the sites the paper's values need. dSPN on+SCH 20190411 cell 1 has only its second pair of sites, which gives 0.584 against the paper's 0.228; with the paper's value the SCH test gives the paper's P (0.0133), without it P = 0.066. iSPN on+sul 20190508 cell 3 has only a distal site; with the paper's 0.217 the sulpiride test gives the paper's P (0.0545), without it P = 0.0097. Under the main basal-ratio rule these two cells decide fig1i-dspn-dendritic-sch-lower and fig3f-ispn-dendritic-sul-no-change; under the stricter rule (0.8 to 1.25) the sulpiride test gives P = 0.0663 without the cell. Reading the gap as data missing is an inference from the recovered P values, as the paper does not list each cell's sites.

The dandiset holds the raw spine image stacks and the rotation videos but no spine counts or rotation counts (none of the 86 spine files has a processing module or analysis entry), the measurements behind Figures 2B, 2C, 4B, 4C, 4K, 6F, 7H, 8A, 9F and 10A. They are only in the paper's Zenodo tables.

The stimulus series of every dendritic sweep (CurrentClampSeries_CellN_Dendritic_Stimulus) is all zero, though the three spikes per sweep show the 2 nA injections were delivered; and the index table gives no kymograph slice for 53 of 997 dendritic sweeps.

In the Sr2+-oEPSC files the light-pulse OptogeneticSeries is all zero in 69 of 140 sweeps, and the intracellular recordings table references no stimulus (its stimulus rows are empty). The pulse time (0.02 s) is only in the optogenetic epochs table.

The GRAB-ACh background reference images are described as taken at zero laser power, but their mean (381 to 525) is above the signal (F0 179 to 355), so they cannot be the PMT background the Methods subtract.

The files cite the bioRxiv preprint (related_publications) and describe the behaviour data with the preprint's figure numbers ("Figure 7J" for the CDGI AIM scores, "Figure 8" for the M1R study), which are Figures 8 and 10 in the published paper the dandiset names.

Patch-clamp subjects are named by recording date (for example Subject20160523LIDOFFeGFP and SubjectRecordedAt20160523000000 for the same day), with no animal identifier, so recordings and spine stacks of one mouse cannot be linked, and the archive has 185 subject folders.

Recomputed on the paper's own per-cell tables, some reported P values differ; the oxo-M test in CDGI KO gives P = 0.47 where the paper reports 0.910, and the rotation test of Figure 8A gives 0.012 where the text reports 0.0092. Others agree closely (0.009766 against 0.0098 for oxo-M in wild type).
18 somatic cells miss one or more current steps between 20 and 300 pA and 14 repeat a step; spike counts for these cells cannot be complete.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)

The stricter 0.8 to 1.25 basal-ratio variant gives P = 0.52.

attempts.paper_title: Individual variability of neural computations underlying flexible decisions
attempts.entry_title: Context-dependent evidence accumulation in rats (Pagan et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Pagan, Tang, Aoi, Pillow, Mante, Sussillo and Brody (2025) on dandiset 001550, which holds the behaviour of 26 rats trained on a task that switches between accumulating location and frequency evidence. It links the dandiset to the paper's published behavioural tables, checks the session statistics and selection, fits the behavioural pulse kernels and their slope indices, tests the optogenetic inactivation, and, with the paper's neural data from GitHub, the link between behavioural and neural slope indices.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Pagan et al. (2025) from dandiset 001550

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's sessions can be linked to the paper's published per-session behavioural tables, and the linked records agree on trial counts, outcomes, evidence and pulse timing.
outcomes.source: Data availability; the paper's data/Sessions_trials at GitHub commit 0ea8fdb
outcomes.notes: Sessions are matched by rat and session name taken from the source file names in the paper's tables. Of 15,278 paper sessions with valid trials, 15,277 (0.9999) are in the dandiset; the missing one, P189 TaskSwitch6-210516a, has 27 valid trials. In all 15,277 the number of valid trials and the fraction correct are equal, and both relative weights agree to 1e-6 in 0.898; of the 1,553 that differ, 861 agree once this attempt's values are capped at 1 as the paper's table does. Of the 692 left, 627 have a missing value on both sides, 5 in the paper's table only, and 60 differ with both values present (median difference 0.87 after capping, not explained); 3 of the 692 are in the paper's selection. In 20 seeded sessions every valid trial agrees on context, correct side, strengths, choice, outcome and position in block, and 0.99996 of 10 ms pulse bins agree. Over every matched session, 627 have an empty per-trial record in the paper's tables; in the other 14,650 the 7,447,692 valid trials agree on every per-trial field and position in block, and 0.99996 of 50 ms pulse bins agree over the 6,532,005 trials whose pulses were binned. The dandiset's Methods selection keeps all 8,843 sessions of the paper's selection plus 6 (5 P187 and P189 sessions not in the paper's tables, and P059 TaskSwitch4-170331a, whose relative weight of 1.112 the paper's table caps at 1.0). Per-rat selected trial counts equal the paper's numhits for 23 of 26 rats and exceed them by 213 (P059), 1,442 (P187) and 609 (P189).
deviations: The paper's `good` flag is not in the dandiset and is not applied; it removes no session that passes the other criteria.

outcomes.statement: The study used 26 male Long-Evans rats, aged between 6 and 24 months.
outcomes.notes: 26 subjects, all male Long Evans, one date of birth each. Ages at the 8,849 selected sessions are 3.0 to 39.1 months (median 15.4); 0.913 lie within 5.4 to 26.4 months and 0.844 within 6 to 24. Eighteen rats have selected sessions before 5.4 months and eight after 26.4. The dates of birth put 25 rats at 1.6 to 2.7 months at their first session in the dandiset; P189 is at 14.1 months, on the day P187 (born 2019-02-21) starts, and its date of birth (2018-02-21) may be a year early.

outcomes.statement: Rats performed on average 542 trials per session.
outcomes.notes: Mean valid trials per session 551.8 over the 8,849 selected sessions (reading b) and 494.2 over all 15,400 task sessions (reading d), both within 487.8 to 596.2. All trials average 817.9 and 749.7 (readings a and c), outside. The 13 unreadable sessions (1 to 3 trials) are left out of readings c and d; added, they give 749.1 and 493.8.
deviations: The Methods do not say which sessions or trials are counted; four readings are shown and two match.

outcomes.statement: On average, rats switched across 14.6 context blocks per session.
outcomes.notes: Blocks per session average 16.98 over selected sessions and 13.90 over all task sessions; switches average 15.98 and 12.90. Blocks over all sessions (13.90) and switches over selected sessions (15.98) are within 13.14 to 16.06; the first is recorded as measured.
deviations: Whether blocks or switches are counted, and over which sessions, is not stated; two of four readings match.

outcomes.statement: Behavioural sessions lasted 2 to 4 hours.
outcomes.notes: Median duration 2.50 h over selected sessions and 2.57 h over all task sessions. Only 0.559 and 0.556 of sessions last 2 to 4 h (0.65 within 1.8 to 4.4); 5% to 95% of selected sessions span 1.26 to 4.41 h, and the range is 0.26 to 7.74 h.
deviations: Duration is taken from the first trial start to the last trial stop; the files hold no session end time.

outcomes.statement: Block switches occurred after a minimum of 30 trials per block, and when a local estimate of performance reached 80% correct.
outcomes.notes: All 141,359 non-final blocks of selected sessions have at least 30 trials counted over all trials (1st percentile 30, median 44); counted over valid trials 0.817 do. Over the last 30 valid trials before a switch the median fraction correct is 0.828 and 0.601 of blocks reach 0.8, so the 80% part is not shown on that window; the task's local estimate is not described.

outcomes.statement: Twenty rats each contributed more than 120,000 trials after training.
outcomes.notes: Twenty rats have more than 120,000 valid trials in selected sessions (the twentieth, P189, has 128,309; the next, P124, 115,123). The same 20 pass at 120,000 or more.

outcomes.statement: After training, choices are mostly driven by location in the location context and by frequency in the frequency context.
outcomes.notes: In all 20 rats both relative weights exceed 0.5; location in the location context 0.770 to 0.860, frequency in the frequency context 0.724 to 0.870.
deviations: Tested by the Methods' logistic regression on generative strengths, not by the four-parameter psychometric fits that the figure shows.

outcomes.statement: Rats switch the feature they attend to within about four trials of a new context block.
outcomes.source: Results, first section; Extended Data Figure 1e (legend panel g)
outcomes.notes: Across 26 rats, at position 4 of a new block the relevant relative weight is 0.91 of its plateau when switching to location and 0.963 when switching to frequency (Methods selection), and 0.914 and 0.961 with the code's 0.65 selection. At position 1 it is 0.502 and 0.560, against plateaus of 0.854 and 0.789. All 26 rats have a fit at positions 1 to 5 (103 to 6,096 trials), so the 30-trial minimum drops nothing. Bootstrapping rats, the position 4 value for the switch to location has a 95% interval of 0.874 to 0.946 and reaches 0.9 in 0.678 of resamples; at position 5, which the criterion also allows, the values are 0.956 and 0.977 and reach 0.9 in 0.998 and 1.000 of resamples.
deviations: The paper's code uses a 0.65 selection for this analysis; the Methods selection is the main result and the code's is a variant.

outcomes.statement: Most rats learned the task in two to five months.
outcomes.source: Results, first section; Extended Data Figure 2g
outcomes.notes: From each rat's first session to its first session with an index of at least 0.7, 17 of 26 rats took 1.8 to 5.5 months (times 0.85 to 8.18 months). With the full selection 19 of 26; counted from the first TaskSwitch session 13 (exactly half) and 17. Within the unwidened 2 to 5 months the counts are 12, 16, 10 and 13. 24 rats start with ProAnti3Marino sessions.
deviations: The paper does not define the start of training or when a rat counts as trained; four pairings of readings are shown, three match.

outcomes.statement: Differential behavioural kernels predominantly converge towards the end of the pulse train, that is the difference between contexts in the weight of a feature shrinks for later pulses.
outcomes.source: Methods, Behavioural logistic regression; Figure 4; Extended Data Figure 3c,f
outcomes.notes: All 36 slope indices of the 18 Figure 4 rats are negative (median -0.432, range -0.774 to -0.097). With the code's fixed penalty of 200 all 36 are negative (median -0.491), and they agree with the indices from the paper's saved weights to at most 0.0177 (r = 0.99973).
deviations: The Methods' ridge penalty is read as the code's penalty on neighbouring weight differences, with its weight chosen by 3-fold cross-validation over 20, 200 and 2000 (chosen weights 20 to 2000); the code fixes it at 200.
The differential kernel is divided by its largest absolute value before the line fit, as the code does; the Methods do not say.

outcomes.statement: Across rats, the shape of the differential behavioural kernel for one feature does not predict the shape for the other feature.
outcomes.source: Results, Linking neural and behaviour variability; Figure 4 top right
outcomes.notes: Across 18 rats r = 0.180 (95% CI -0.313 to 0.597), p = 0.475; with the fixed penalty r = 0.092, p = 0.717; from the paper's saved weights r = 0.094, p = 0.71.
deviations: The paper gives no test; a two-sided Pearson correlation was chosen before the analysis.

outcomes.statement: The behavioural slope index computed from the first half of a rat's trials is correlated with the index from the second half (r = 0.58, p = 0.000013).
outcomes.notes: Over 24 rats and 48 values r = 0.552 (95% CI 0.318 to 0.723), p = 4.7e-05, within 0.522 to 0.638. With the fixed penalty r = 0.577, p = 1.8e-05. Location alone r = 0.470, frequency alone r = 0.736.
deviations: The halves use the penalty weight chosen on all of that rat's trials in that context.

outcomes.statement: Bilateral optogenetic silencing of the frontal orienting fields during the stimulus impairs performance of the task (three rats).
outcomes.source: Results, first section; Extended Data Figure 4g
outcomes.notes: Four rats have opto sessions (P116 47, P124 74, P127 4 and P131 88 with at least 100 valid trials). With bilateral full-trial epochs accuracy is lower than on control trials in the same sessions with p < 0.05 in 2 of the 3 rats with most sessions, P116 (0.639 against 0.733, 873 trials, p below 1e-4) and P131 (0.686 against 0.727, 1,988 trials, p = 0.0001). P124 is higher (0.712 against 0.687, p = 0.17) and P127 lower but not significantly (0.603 against 0.634, p = 0.55). Any bilateral epoch gives 2 of 3 and 2 of 4 as well. Every trial with an epoch has the laser connected; with laser-connected trials only the accuracies and p values are the same.
deviations: The paper does not say which three rats were analysed, which sessions, or its test; the readings and the Fisher test were chosen before the analysis.

outcomes.statement: The neurons in the paper's published neural data can be linked to the dandiset's rats and sessions; they come from 199 sessions of 7 rats.
outcomes.source: Results, first section (n = 199 sessions, n = 7 rats); the paper's data/neural_data and data/rat_for_each_neuron.mat at GitHub commit 0ea8fdb
outcomes.notes: All 7 rats are in the dandiset and every cell file names one of them. Under the criterion's rule (the cell's trials equal a contiguous run of one session's valid trials) 2,371 of 3,495 cells (0.678) match one session and none matches more than one; they come from 110 sessions against 199. With gaps allowed (a variant) 3,269 cells (0.935) match exactly one session, from 112 sessions; 226 cells match none, 189 of them P100's. The neural files leave out some trials of a session, so the contiguous rule is stricter than needed, but neither rule finds 199 sessions. Searching every TaskSwitch protocol (adding P100's 13 TaskSwitch4repeat sessions) gives 2,425 contiguous matches (0.694) from 113 sessions and 3,349 with gaps (0.958) from 115; the 146 cells left share a median 0.43 of their 8-trial windows with their best session, and 61 of those 64 best sessions are already matched.
deviations: The neural files carry no session identifier; cells are matched by their trial sequence.

outcomes.statement: The recordings yielded 3,495 putative single units, 2,047, 832, 258, 94 and 54 from five rats in FOF and 112 and 98 from two rats in mPFC.
outcomes.source: Results, first section; Methods, Analysis of neural data
outcomes.notes: The cell files hold 3,495 units, FOF 2,047 (P100), 832 (P059), 258 (P055), 94 (P095) and 54 (P049), mPFC 112 (P101) and 98 (P102), and rat_for_each_neuron.mat agrees with every file. The Methods sentence that puts all 3,495 in FOF counts the 210 mPFC units as well.

outcomes.statement: Neural slope indices vary across rats and features, with no apparent correlation between the location and frequency indices across the seven recorded rats.
outcomes.source: Results, Pulse analyses distinguish solutions; Figure 3h
outcomes.notes: Neural slope indices range from -0.221 to 1.728 (location) and 0.465 to 1.500 (frequency); across the 7 rats r = -0.177 (95% CI -0.821 to 0.665), p = 0.704. The Methods say differential pulse responses only showed positive (or zero) slope indices; three location indices here are negative (P049 -0.221, P101 -0.045, P095 -0.007). The criterion does not test this.
deviations: The per-neuron kernels are the paper's fitted ones from its repository; the GLM was not refitted from spikes.
The paper gives no test; a two-sided Pearson correlation was chosen before the analysis.

outcomes.statement: Choice axes estimated separately in the two contexts are essentially parallel (average angle 1.6 degrees, not different from 0 in 6 of 7 rats).
outcomes.source: Results, first section; Extended Data Figure 5
outcomes.notes: By ExtDataFigure5ag.m on the paper's per-context kernels, the angle the code plots (the two context choice axes projected on the first 3 principal components of both contexts' choice kernels, folded to at most 90 degrees) is 5.53, 7.91, 4.49, 1.82, 1.12, 4.25 and 8.00 degrees (P049, P055, P059, P095, P100, P101, P102), mean 4.73, against the reported 1.6 (tolerance 1.44 to 1.76); no rat is in the tolerance. The 3 components explain 0.85 to 0.94 of the variance. The full-space angle, which the code computes first and overwrites, averages 40.34 (29.43 folded). All units of each rat have fits in both contexts. The reported test against 0 (not different from 0 in 6 of 7 rats) is a permutation test the Methods describe, shuffling the trials' context labels and recomputing both axes; it is not in the repository's code and needs the per-neuron kernels refitted for every shuffle, so it was not run.
deviations: The criterion was corrected after the first verification round to follow the angle the code plots; it first described only the full-space angle, now a variant. Both are outside the tolerance.

outcomes.statement: The behavioural slope index and the neural slope index are anti-correlated across rats and features (r = -0.73, P < 0.01), and for location (r = -0.71) and frequency (r = -0.71) alone (P < 0.1).
outcomes.source: Results, Linking neural and behaviour variability; Figure 5d
outcomes.notes: Behavioural slope indices from the dandiset (Methods selection, bins 14 to 26) against neural indices from the paper's kernels give r = -0.697 over 14 values (95% CI -0.896 to -0.264), p = 0.0056, within -0.803 to -0.657. Location alone r = -0.675 (p = 0.096), frequency alone r = -0.772 (p = 0.042); the paper reports -0.71 for each with P < 0.1, and both hold at that level. With the code's 0.65 and 0.6 selection and penalty 200, r = -0.765 (p = 0.0014), and the paper's saved behavioural indices give -0.768. The match of neurons to rats, which this claim needs, holds for every cell; the session-level link that fails in neural-link is not used here.
deviations: The Methods selection keeps 23,014 and 25,847 trials of P049 and P059 against 135,001 and 162,317 under the code's selection, and their location indices change sign (0.131 against -0.432, 1.292 against -0.613).
Neural kernels are the paper's fitted ones, not refitted from spikes.

The result is close to the tolerance and depends on P049 and P059. With those two rats from the code's selection r = -0.834, and with the code's selection and cross-validated penalty r = -0.830, both beyond the tolerance on the negative side; leaving out one rat at a time gives -0.655 to -0.895, inside the tolerance for 4 of 7. All five 14-point correlations shown are negative with p < 0.01.

outcomes.statement: Choice-related population activity in FOF evolves along an essentially one-dimensional line during the stimulus (73.3% of variance; 81.3% for the two-dimensional choice subspace).
outcomes.notes: Figure1e.m projects the per-context choice kernels on principal components but computes neither 81.3% nor 73.3%, and the text does not say which kernels, time window or normalisation the percentages refer to. The data (combined_kernels_per_context.mat, and the mTDR fits in data/Arrays_Pagan) are public in the paper's repository.

outcomes.statement: In FOF, trajectories for different evidence strengths separate along each sensory axis whether the feature is relevant or irrelevant, so irrelevant information is not gated out before frontal cortex.
outcomes.notes: Needs the mTDR fits of the MATLAB toolbox in the repository's mbtdr folder (with minFunc) on data/Arrays_Pagan. MATLAB cannot be installed in the entry's locked Python environment and the toolbox was not ported.

outcomes.statement: RNNs trained by backpropagation through time favour selection vector modulation.
outcomes.notes: Needs 1,000 RNNs trained by backpropagation through time (train_model.py in flexible_decision_making_rnn at commit 13cd245) and their linearisation; the repository holds three trained models. Training them is far beyond the 30-minute limit.

outcomes.statement: In RNNs engineered across the solution space, neural and behavioural slope indices are tightly anti-correlated.
outcomes.notes: The engineered RNNs and their pulse and behavioural kernels are built by MATLAB scripts (handcraft_model.m and others in flexible_decision_making_rnn at commit 13cd245), which cannot run in the entry's environment and were not ported.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the behaviour. The electrophysiology behind Figures 1d to 1f, 3h and 5d (3,495 units from 7 rats) is not in it; it is public only in the paper's GitHub repository, as one MATLAB file per unit with binned spike counts, without raw data or spike sorting output.

Nothing links the paper's units to dandiset sessions. Matched by trial sequence, 3,269 of 3,495 units fall in exactly one dandiset session when gaps are allowed (2,371 without gaps), from 112 sessions, where the paper reports 199; 226 units match no session. Searching every TaskSwitch protocol gives 3,349 units from 115 sessions, and 146 unmatched.
Every optogenetic epoch gives a wavelength of 473 nm; Extended Data Figure 4 says 450 nm, and the conversion's documentation says the value was corrected to 450.
Optogenetic epochs are present for four rats (P116, P124, P127, P131), where the paper reports three; nothing in the dandiset or the paper says which three were analysed.

The dates of birth give ages of 3.0 to 39.1 months at the sessions the paper's selection keeps (18 rats younger than 5.4 months at some), where the Methods state 6 to 24 months. Either the dates of birth or the stated ages are wrong. The dates of birth put 25 rats at 1.6 to 2.7 months at their first session; P189's (2018-02-21) puts it at 14.1 months on the day P187, born 2019-02-21, starts, and may be a year early.

Thirteen task sessions (1 to 3 trials each) lack HistorySection_result_history or a pulse column, and 95 of the other 15,400 lack HistorySection_hit_history. Where both outcome columns exist they agree on every trial.
One session of the paper's tables with 27 valid trials, P189 TaskSwitch6-210516a, is not in the dandiset; the conversion's notes list it among aborted sessions left out.
Six task sessions of P187 and P189 (TaskSwitch6, 2021) are in the dandiset but not in the paper's tables; five of them pass the Methods selection, adding 1,442 and 609 trials to those rats.
HistorySection_gammafreq_history, a signed strength, is stored as uint8 or int16 in 570 files; in all of them its values equal the float gamma_freq, so nothing was lost.

The paper's code also requires a per-session `good` flag that the Methods do not describe and the dandiset does not hold, and caps relative weights at 1; neither changes the selection except for one P059 session.

The Methods describe ridge regression with the regulariser chosen by cross-validation; the code adds a fixed penalty of 200 on squared differences of neighbouring weights. The code also uses looser selections (0.65 correct and 0.6 index) for the recorded rats in Figure 5d and for Extended Data Figure 1e than the Methods' 0.7.

The paper's own code (ExtDataFigure5ag.m), applied to its own fitted per-context kernels, gives angles of 1.1 to 8.0 degrees between the context choice axes (mean 4.7), not the reported average of 1.6 degrees. The permutation test of each angle against 0 that the Methods describe is not in the code.

The Methods say 3,495 units were recorded from 5 rats in FOF and list FOF counts that sum to 3,285; the 3,495 include the 210 mPFC units. The main text calls a converging differential behavioural kernel a slope index above 0, while the Methods and the code give converging kernels negative indices, as the data have.
