attempts.paper_title: Microinvasive Probes for Monitoring Electrical and Chemical Neural Activity in Nonhuman Primates
attempts.entry_title: Microinvasive probes for dopamine, LFP and spikes in monkeys (Amjad et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Amjad, Mahajan, Choi, Shrivastav, Murray, Somich, Coyne and Schwerdt (2025) on dandiset 002013, which holds the three example sessions of the paper. It checks the recording parameters and task structure, the dopamine response to large and small reward cues at site c8dg, beta-band LFP suppression by reward and cue side at c3bs-c3a, beta bursts around the cue, and the isolation of the sorted unit of monkey P, and compares the dandiset with the paper's Zenodo deposit.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Amjad et al. (2025) from dandiset 002013

outcomes.statement: Insertion yields were low, 21.4% (3 of 14 sensors) in monkey T and 33% (3 of 9) in monkey P, counted as recording sites that stayed functional after insertion until the end of the study.
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds one or two sites per session and no list of the implanted sensors or of which kept working, in its files or its metadata. None of the ten file names of the paper's Zenodo deposit, printed in the data check, points to such a list.

outcomes.statement: The s-µIPs kept recording for more than a year after implantation; the example sites were recorded 483 days (c8dg), 496 days (c3bs-c3a) and 390 days (monkey P) after implantation.
outcomes.source: Figure 3 to 5 legends; Results and Discussion
outcomes.notes: The subject, device and electrode fields of the files hold no implantation date, and none of the mentions of implantation in the files' general section or the dandiset metadata (all printed in the data check) comes with a date, so days post-implant cannot be computed. The two Monkey T sessions are 13 days apart, which matches the difference between the 483 and 496 days of the legends.

outcomes.statement: FSCV applied a triangular waveform from -0.4 to 1.3 V at 400 V/s, every 100 ms (10 Hz).
outcomes.notes: The applied voltage runs from -0.347 to 1.340 V at 400.5 V/s, one scan every 0.1 s. Three of four values are within tolerance; the lowest potential is outside -0.4 +- 0.04 V. The dandiset's own description (-0.35 to 1.34 V) agrees with the data, so the Methods state the nominal waveform. The data of the applied voltage have conversion 1 and offset 0, so the values are read as stored.
deviations: Measured on session 09/13/2024 only, the only FSCV session in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: EPhys was sampled at 30 kHz in monkey P and 32 kHz in monkey T, and band-pass filtered from 0.1 to 7500 Hz.
outcomes.notes: Monkey P's raw timestamps have a median interval of 33.333 µs (30 kHz) and Monkey T's series a rate of 32000 Hz. The Neuralynx settings of both Monkey T channels give a low cut of 0.1 Hz and a high cut of 8000 Hz, inside the tolerance of 7500 Hz but not equal to it; the dandiset's description also says 0.1 to 7500 Hz (printed). Monkey P's file stores no filter settings; its notes, printed in full, and its electrode columns name no filter or cut-off.

outcomes.statement: In the shape task, forced trials made up 25% of all trials, and the cue-reward association was reversed after blocks of 50 to 300 trials.
outcomes.notes: Forced trials are 358 of 1468 (24.4%). The eight complete blocks of the cue-reward association are 71 to 273 trials long; the first and last blocks, cut by the file, are 61 and 194 trials.
deviations: Blocks are found from the image codes of successful forced trials, as choice trials carry no feedback code; a reversal is placed after the last forced trial of the earlier association, so block edges are uncertain by the gap between forced trials.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset reproduces the processed data the paper deposited on Zenodo; the trial selections and the beta power of the paper's example trial computed from the dandiset agree with the paper's own files.
outcomes.notes: Trials are matched by number. The decoded selections agree with the four Zenodo lists for 569 of 570, 602 of 602, 594 of 594 and 577 of 578 trials; the only difference is trial 1501, the last of the session, absent from the Zenodo large-reward and right lists. The Zenodo example "trial35" is the 35th trial of the large-reward list (trial 84). Beta power computed here correlates with its trace at r = 0.943 at a lag of 6 ms, with a median amplitude ratio of 0.943, so the dandiset's LFP, its trial times and the beta pipeline used here agree with the paper's files. The Zenodo example's raw LFP variable is a copy of its time variable, so the LFP trace itself could not be compared. The criterion tests only r and was written after r = 0.94 was known. The amplitudes differ (maximum 2184 µV² here against 1560 µV² in the Zenodo trace), so the paper's filter or envelope probably differs from the one used here.
deviations: The beta filter (4th-order Butterworth, forwards and backwards, squared Hilbert envelope) is a common choice; the paper's code is not public, and r = 0.943 suggests its filter differs somewhat.

outcomes.statement: Dopamine was measured from two neighbouring channels of one dual-channel s-µIP (sites c8dg and c8ds, 0.1 to 0.2 mm apart), and both showed dopamine increases after the value cue in a single forced large-reward trial.
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds FSCV from site c8dg only. Site c8ds is not in it, and the Zenodo deposit holds processed FSCV of c8dg only; its one FSCV file is FSCV_trlists_c8dg_09132024_firsthalf.mat (file list printed in the data check). The c8dg half can be tested and holds; the mean of the re-referenced dopamine over 0 to 3 s is above zero in 56 of 85 large-reward forced trials (65.9%), and in 58 of 85 with a baseline of the mean over -1 to 0 s.

outcomes.statement: The single-trial FSCV colour plot shows dopamine redox current, with changes near 0.6 V (oxidation) and -0.2 V (reduction) after the value cue.
outcomes.notes: The raw FSCV current is in the dandiset, but its timing could not be linked to the trials. Its scan times are an exact 0.1 s grid starting at the first trial start and running 24120 s, past the last trial; at 0.6 V it does not match the stored oxidation current of any of six rows tested at the stored times (|r| below 0.06) or anywhere in the record (best r 0.16 to 0.20 at offsets that differ from row to row); and it shows no large-against-small contrast at the stored value cue times (p = 0.46). The same search at 0.50 V, 0.70 V and -0.19 V gives best r 0.17 to 0.22 at offsets that differ from row to row. Computed at the stored times (not deciding), the background-subtracted voltammogram of 164 large-reward forced trials has its largest rising-sweep value at -0.24 V (at 0.6 V it is -0.033) and its most negative value at the switching potential, 1.34 V, with an SD of 0.042 over the scan; it does not meet the criterion. A colour plot of a forced large-reward trial therefore cannot be placed in the trial.

outcomes.statement: Single-trial bipolar LFP from site c3bs-c3a shows beta bursts (one to a few cycles of high beta power) whose frequency changes around the cue and other task events.
outcomes.notes: With the threshold at the 75th percentile (356 µV²) and bursts of at least 50 ms, the burst rate of 570 large-reward trials is 1.51 per s in the second before the value cue and 1.21 in the second after it (Wilcoxon p = 9.5e-10). The rate changes around the cue at the 50th and 90th percentiles too (p below 1e-40), rising at the 50th and falling at the 90th, so its direction depends on the threshold while the change does not. The rate dips just after the cue (0.51 per s in 0 to 0.25 s) and falls again from 6 s after it, after the feedback. On the smoothed power 95.1% of runs above the 75th percentile last at least 50 ms (median 206 ms), so the minimum length does little; on the unsmoothed envelope the rate also falls after the cue (3.07 to 2.11 per s, p = 6.8e-34). At the deciding threshold the fall in bursts coincides with the drop in beta power after the cue, so it is not separate evidence from the suppression of fig4b-beta-reward.
deviations: The paper shows a single trial and does not define a burst; the threshold, minimum length and test were chosen here before the analysis.

outcomes.statement: Trial-averaged dopamine at site c8dg is higher after large-reward than after small-reward value cues, in successful forced trials of the shape task.
outcomes.notes: Over 0 to 3 s after the value cue, the re-referenced dopamine has a median of 1.28 in 85 large-reward trials and 0.19 in 80 small-reward trials (Mann-Whitney p = 0.023; 3 trials of 168 have no valid samples in the window). The difference lies in 1.5 to 3 s (p = 0.0072), not 0 to 1.5 s (p = 0.41). The effect is weak. Before the cue the groups differ the other way (p = 0.064). Without re-referencing (the stored da) there is no difference (p = 0.3), nor in the re-referenced oxidation current (p = 0.41). It holds in trials 1 to 367 (p = 0.013) and not in trials 368 to 734 (p = 0.51). With a baseline of the mean over -1 to 0 s in place of the sample at the cue the result is the same (1.38 against 0.10, p = 0.022).
deviations: Only the first 734 of 1468 trials of the session have trial-aligned FSCV in the dandiset, so 168 successful forced trials are used.

The stored da is not referenced at the value cue; it is re-referenced here by subtracting its value at the cue, which equals background subtraction there only if the PCA projection was linear and the nulling (NaN) masks are ignored.
Small reward is inferred from the absence of the big-reward code, confirmed by the cue condition codes 35 and 36 in all 303 successful forced trials.
The paper gives no window or test; 0 to 3 s and the Mann-Whitney test were chosen before the analysis.

outcomes.statement: Beta-band LFP power at c3bs-c3a in the direction task is more suppressed (stronger event-related desynchronization) after large-reward than after small-reward value cues, in a brief window after the cue.
outcomes.notes: Over 0 to 0.5 s after the value cue, median beta power is 275 µV² in 570 large-reward trials and 327 µV² in 602 small-reward trials (ratio 0.84, Mann-Whitney p = 1e-08), with no difference before the cue (ratio 1.006, p = 0.82). It holds relative to pre-cue power (ratio 0.82, p = 1.1e-06) and on each side (left p = 0.0016, right p = 1e-07). It is confined to a brief window, as the legend says; over 0 to 1 s large is slightly higher (ratio 1.04, p = 0.09) and over 0.25 to 0.75 s there is no difference (p = 0.66). The 0.25 s smoothing does not carry the difference from before the cue; on the unsmoothed envelope it holds over 0 to 0.5 s (ratio 0.834, p = 1.9e-08) and 0.125 to 0.5 s (ratio 0.671, p = 4.8e-19); in 0.1 s bins large and small do not differ before the cue (ratios 0.95 to 1.05), large is lower from 0.1 to 0.4 s (0.85, 0.59, 0.60) and higher from 0.5 s on (1.32 to 1.49). The criterion, lower power over 0 to 0.5 s, is met; the bins fit a deeper suppression after large-reward cues and equally an earlier suppression with an earlier rebound, so the part of the claim saying the suppression is greater is not shown. The LFP's 1497 joins do not step (largest change at a join 20.3 µV, below the 99.9th percentile of 26.0 µV over all samples), and 118 of 1172 successful trials have one within -0.5 to 1 s of the cue, 23 to 36 in each reward and side condition. Trial 1501, absent from the Zenodo lists, is included; one trial of 570 cannot change the result.
deviations: The paper does not give the window highlighted in Figure 4B or a test; 0 to 0.5 s and the Mann-Whitney test were chosen before the analysis.

outcomes.statement: With the reward fixed at large, beta-band LFP power is more suppressed when the cue is on the left (contralateral) than on the right (ipsilateral).
outcomes.notes: Among large-reward trials, median beta power over 0 to 0.5 s is 245 µV² for left cues and 301 µV² for right cues (282 and 288 trials, ratio 0.81, Mann-Whitney p = 1.6e-06). Before the cue left is slightly higher (ratio 1.095, p = 0.013), so relative to pre-cue power the difference is larger (ratio 0.71, p = 2.1e-09). It holds over 0 to 1 s (p = 0.019), not over 0.25 to 0.75 s (p = 0.75), and also in small-reward trials (p = 1.5e-10). On the unsmoothed envelope left is lower over 0 to 0.5 s (ratio 0.807, p = 1.7e-06) and 0.125 to 0.5 s (ratio 0.688, p = 3.2e-17), most from 0.1 to 0.3 s (ratios 0.54 and 0.55).
deviations: Left is taken as contralateral, as the Methods state; the files do not say which hemisphere was implanted.
Window and test chosen before the analysis, as for fig4b-beta-reward.

outcomes.statement: Spikes recorded from an s-µIP in the caudate of monkey P (site c33, 390 days post implant) fire at a different rate for large and small reward during the value cue fixation of the direction task.
outcomes.notes: Monkey P's file has no trials table and no events, so value cue times and reward sizes are not in the dandiset. The paper's Zenodo deposit has the session's raw Neuralynx events (session126_events.mat) as TTL values without names; their codes differ from those of the Monkey T sessions, so they could not be decoded (metadata insufficient). The notebook now reads that file, with 20812 events with 36 distinct TTL values and no names; the trial-start code 128 does not occur and the value cue code 23 occurs 20 times.

outcomes.statement: The s-µIP recorded a spike-sorted unit in monkey P, shown by its average waveform and its interspike interval histogram.
outcomes.notes: Plexon unit 1 has 31247 spikes at 2.61 Hz. One of 31246 interspike intervals is under 1 ms (0.003%), and its mean waveform trough (-30.6 µV) is 5.66 times the raw noise level (5.41 µV, 300 to 6000 Hz, 600 s). The units table's unit 0 (unsorted and poor-quality spikes merged) has 11.65% of intervals under 1 ms and is not a unit.
deviations: The noise level and the two thresholds are common choices; the paper shows the waveform and histogram without numbers.
The paper names the site c33; the file names it cl3. The session is taken as the paper's.

findings.statement: Each event is stored about five times in the events tables of both Monkey T sessions (85665 stored times, 17686 distinct, in 09/13/2024; 59702 and 12434 in 09/26/2024), once for every overlapping 60 s trial window that contains it.

The trials tables hold only times, no trial conditions. Conditions must be decoded from the event codes. Session 09/13/2024 has no small-reward code, and the labels of codes 35 and 36 ("right cue reward condition 1/2") do not say that they code large and small reward, which the data show in all 303 successful forced trials.

The trial-aligned FSCV table of session 09/13/2024 has rows for only the first 734 of its 1468 trials (from a source file named "firsthalf"), and the dandiset has FSCV from c8dg only; the second site of Figure 3A (c8ds) is missing.
The trial-aligned FSCV columns (da, ph, m, iox) carry no units, and da is not referenced at the value cue as the Methods describe; the reference point is not stated.
The raw FSCV current is labelled amperes, but its values range from -1527 to 1557; the unit is likely nA or the data are not current.

The raw FSCV scan times are an exact 0.1 s grid starting at the first trial start and running 24120 s, past the last trial, and the raw current cannot be matched to the trial-aligned oxidation current at any offset or to the task at the stored times. The conversion notes say the times were interpolated between trial-start codes; the data do not support that they are on the trial clock.
The bipolar LFP of session 09/26/2024 stores values already in volts (around 1e-4) with a conversion factor of 3.05e-8, so that read as NWB prescribes it is in picovolts.

The raw ephys of session 09/26/2024 has starting_time 0 and no timestamps, but it matches the stored LFP (r 0.92 to 0.98) only when read 9831.35 s later on the trial clock, consistently from the first trial to the last.

In Monkey P's file the spike times (6800 to 18785 s) are 6800.666 s later than the raw signal's timestamps (0 to 11985 s); the spike-triggered average of the raw signal shows the spike only with that shift. The file does not say the two use different clocks.

In Monkey P's units table, unit 0 merges the unsorted (0) and poor-quality (-1) thresholded spikes, including 7 spike times below 1 s and 3 repeated times; the poor-quality spikes of the thresholded table are not in time order.
Monkey P's file has no trials or events, so the reward-related firing of Figure 5A cannot be tested. The paper's Zenodo events for this session are raw TTL values without a code map.
No implantation dates are given, so the days post-implant of each session cannot be checked.

Monkey P's site is named cl3 in the file and dandiset description, c33 in the Figure 5 legend; the files' related_publications cite the bioRxiv preprint, not the article; the acquisition high cut is 8000 Hz in the Neuralynx settings, not the 7500 Hz the description states.
The applied FSCV waveform runs from -0.347 to 1.340 V, as the dandiset description says; the paper's Methods give -0.4 to 1.3 V.

attempts.paper_title: Aseptic, semi-sealed cranial chamber implants for chronic multi-channel neurochemical and electrophysiological neural recording in nonhuman primates
attempts.entry_title: Dopamine, spikes and LFP through an aseptic cranial chamber in a rhesus monkey (Choi et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the recording findings of Choi et al. (2025) on dandiset 002014, which holds one session of monkey T recorded through the paper's semi-sealed chamber. It compares dopamine and beta-band LFP power between large and small reward trials, aligns spikes to the value cue, and checks the unit's waveform and interspike intervals. The surgical, culture, drainage and yield results, and monkey J, are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Choi et al. (2025) from dandiset 002014

outcomes.statement: In a single trial (trial 133 of the session), dopamine concentration changes at site c8ds fluctuate, especially after the value cue display.
outcomes.notes: In trial 133 (1-based, a successful large reward trial) the SD of dopamine referenced at V over the 5 s after V is 2.02 times that over the 5 s before. Under the other reading (index 133, trial 134) the ratio is 2.04, with 36% and 46% of samples NaN. The test is weak. Of the 889 successful trials with a reference at V, the median ratio is 1.27, 64% exceed 1, and trial 133's ratio is above 76.9% of them. The criterion was written after trial 133's values had been printed.
deviations: The paper shows the trial as a figure with no measure; the SD ratio and its windows were chosen here.
The paper's trial numbering is not stated; both 1-based and 0-based readings are shown, and both match.

outcomes.statement: Trial-averaged dopamine at site c8ds, aligned to the value cue, increases more for large than for small reward trials, especially between the value cue display and reward.
outcomes.notes: From V to reward, dopamine referenced at V averages 1.88 in large and 1.10 in small reward trials (difference 0.78 in the file's unstated unit, Cohen's d 0.19, Mann-Whitney p = 0.0035, 429 and 460 trials, 23 and 39 dropped for lack of a reference at V). Shuffling the labels within blocks of 50 consecutive trials, which keeps the drift across the session in the null, gives p = 0.0045. The difference is small in the first 2 s after V (p = 0.44) and largest from reward to 3 s after (difference 1.59, p = 0.0001, within blocks p = 0.0010); before V there is none (p = 0.50). It holds in the second half of the session (p = 0.0125) and not significantly in the first (p = 0.075). Without trial 1411, p = 0.0031.
deviations: The PCA dopamine estimate at V is subtracted, in place of subtracting the background voltammogram at V before the PCA; the two agree if the PCA model is linear, which the dandiset does not let us check.
The window (V to each trial's reward) and the test were chosen here; the paper states none.
Trial 1411, which the paper's large reward list leaves out, is included (one trial of 452); without it p = 0.0031.
Where dopamine is NaN at V, the reference is interpolated between the nearest valid samples if both lie within 0.2 s; none of the 62 such trials has them, so all are dropped.

outcomes.statement: Spikes recorded at site c5d on a chamber-implanted CFE can be shown as a raster and a peristimulus time histogram aligned to the value cue display, for large and small reward trials.
outcomes.source: Figure 9A and its legend; Results, section 3.5
outcomes.notes: With the spike times moved to the trial clock by the offset measured in the data check (11812.11 s), all successful trials have a spike within V - 1 s to V + 3 s, and the variance across 100 ms bins of the PSTH is 0.49 against a 95th percentile of 0.06 over random alignments (p = 0.005 with 200); 0.48 with the 7 ms lag also corrected. The rate falls from 5.63 spikes/s before V to 4.58 in the first 0.2 s and rises to 7.70 at 0.3 to 0.5 s. Large and small trials do not differ over 0 to 1 s (5.69 against 5.66 spikes/s, p = 0.90); the paper states no difference. The Plexon unit gives 0.17 against 0.06. With the spike times as stored, 42% of trials have a spike in the window and the variance is 0.01 against 0.03, so the claim fails on the file as published.
deviations: The spike times are moved by an offset measured from the data (the raw ephys located in the stored LFP); the file places them 11812.11 s early.
The spikes are those of the thresholded table (the paper's Zenodo file); the Plexon unit is a variant.
The paper states no effect for this panel; the criterion (spikes in most trials, and a rate locked to V beyond chance) was chosen here.

outcomes.statement: The spikes at site c5d have a consistent waveform (mean and standard deviation) and an interspike interval distribution (1 ms bins) consistent with a single unit.
outcomes.notes: The criterion holds, but the evidence for a single unit is weak. No ISI is under 1 ms (9 of 101732 under 2 ms), and the mean waveform's trough of -56.4 µV is 4.79 times the SD across spikes at that sample. Neither part could easily fail. The shortest ISI, 1.562 ms, just exceeds the 48-sample (1.50 ms) waveform, so the detector's dead time excludes ISIs under 1 ms, and every one of the 101733 spikes exceeds the 40 µV threshold (smallest peak 40.3 µV), which nearly forces the trough above twice the SD. Above the dead time, ISIs per ms at 1.56 to 3 ms are 0.106 times those at 10 to 30 ms (Plexon unit 0.204), which fits a refractory period in most spikes but does not rule out other units. Only 54411 of the Plexon unit's 90912 spikes lie within 0.2 ms of a spike of thresholded unit 1 (101733 spikes). The Plexon unit has 1 ISI under 1 ms, 14 (0.015%) under 1.56 ms and 39 (0.04%) under 2 ms.
deviations: The paper states no measure for these panels; the 1% ISI rule and the trough-to-SD ratio are common choices made here.
The waveforms are read as microvolts, although the file states volts.

outcomes.statement: Trial-averaged beta-band LFP power at c7b referenced to c5c is suppressed more in the brief window after the value cue for large than for small reward cues.
outcomes.notes: Beta power (13 to 30 Hz) falls after V in both conditions (median log10 ratio of 0 to 0.5 s after V to 0.5 s before, -0.158 for large and -0.125 for small, each p < 0.001 against 0). The fall is larger for large cues, but not significantly (difference of medians -0.033, Mann-Whitney p = 0.108; 452 and 499 trials, none dropped; shuffling within blocks of 50 trials, p = 0.19). Averaged over trials, as in the paper's figure, power over 0 to 0.5 s is 0.839 of the baseline for large (95% CI 0.782 to 0.903) and 0.885 for small (0.831 to 0.940), a difference of -0.046 (-0.125 to 0.036). No variant reaches p < 0.05 (15 to 30 Hz, p = 0.063; 1 s baseline, p = 0.108; 12 to 25 Hz, p = 0.19; windows of 0 to 0.3 s and 0 to 1 s, p = 0.59 and 0.84; without baseline, p = 0.17). The paper states no test for this panel.
deviations: The band, the filter, the power measure, the baseline, the window and the test were chosen here; the paper gives none.
The stored series, described as beta-band LFP, is broadband and was band-passed here.

outcomes.statement: The chamber system provided recordings of dopamine and electrical neural activity in two monkeys (T and J).
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds one session of monkey T only (one NWB file). No recording of monkey J is in it or in the paper's Zenodo record, which also holds monkey T only. The monkey T part is tested by the Figure 8 and 9 claims.

outcomes.statement: 53% (21/40) and 25% (13/51) of implanted sCFEs retained functionality (background current above 500 nA and noise below 0.05 nA) in monkeys T and J.
outcomes.notes: The per-electrode background current and noise measured at implantation and during recovery, for 40 and 51 sCFEs, are not in the dandiset, which holds one FSCV electrode (c8ds) on one day. Not found in the Zenodo record either.

outcomes.statement: 73% (29/40) and 39% (20/51) of implanted sCFEs retained background current above 500 nA in monkeys T and J, of which 28% and 35% had noise above 0.05 nA.
outcomes.notes: As for scfe-functional-yield; the electrode-level background and noise measurements are not deposited.

outcomes.statement: 21.4% (3/14) and 14.2% (2/14) of mCFEs retained functionality in monkeys T and J.
outcomes.notes: No mCFE measurements are in the dandiset or the Zenodo record.

outcomes.statement: Of the functional CFEs, 63% (15/24) and 53% (8/15) in monkeys T and J displayed visible dopamine signals and were used during task performance.
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds the FSCV of one electrode; the 24 and 15 functional CFEs and which of them showed dopamine signals are not deposited.

outcomes.statement: Monkey T kept negative bacterial cultures for all samples; in monkey J, staphylococcus cultured at 29 days post-implant was cleared by 39 to 44 days and the chamber stayed aseptic for 286 days after treatment.
outcomes.notes: The culture results (IDEXX BioAnalytics) are not in the dandiset, the Zenodo record or the protocols.io protocols the paper cites.

outcomes.statement: Fluid aspirated from the chamber per session ranged from 0.3 to 4.8 mL in monkey T and 0.2 to 9.8 mL in monkey J, and was sanguinous for the first 18 (T) and 217 (J) days.
outcomes.notes: The aspirated volumes per session are not in the dandiset or the Zenodo record.

outcomes.statement: Bone growth was observed within and around the chamber in both monkeys, and the chamber margins stayed relatively healthy.
outcomes.notes: The observations are photographs and surgical notes, which are not deposited.

findings.statement: The raw ephys and the spike times are not on the clock of the trials, events, LFP and FSCV table. The raw ephys is stored with a starting time of 0 s and a rate, and the spike times count from its first sample. Locating the raw c7b minus c5c signal in the stored LFP puts raw time 0 at 11812.11 s on the trial clock (correlation 0.98 to 1.00 at eight points, drift about 4 ms per hour). Without this correction spikes cannot be aligned to the task. The dandiset description says all data are expressed relative to the start of the Neuralynx recording, which the data contradict.

The absolute times disagree. On the trial clock the raw samples run from 12:06:44 to 17:12:20, while the Neuralynx header gives the recording as opened at 08:49:52 (the session start) and closed at 15:12:24, two hours before the raw samples end. The header span (22952 s) is also longer than the raw samples (18336 s).

The stored spike times of the thresholded units are about 7.1 ms after the spike troughs in raw c5d (in one 300 s segment of 1633 spikes, per-spike trough lags of -7.4 to -6.9 ms from the 10th to the 90th percentile, 98.8% within 0.5 ms of -7.1 ms).

The series "bipolar_lfp_series" is described as beta-band LFP but is broadband with line noise removed. Its values are already in volts, while it carries the raw int16 conversion factor (3.05e-8), which would scale them about 3e7 times too small.
The thresholded spike waveforms are stated in volts but hold microvolts (mean trough about -56), and the raw FSCV current is stated in amperes but holds nanoamperes (values around 1000).
The columns of the trial-aligned FSCV table (da, ph, m, iox) state no units, and the `good` column is true for every trial.

The subject description ("Two adult female rhesus monkeys were used for in vivo validation of the s-µIP device"), the session and experiment descriptions and the keyword "micro-invasive neural implant" describe the lab's micro-invasive probe study, not this paper's chamber.

The event table stores each event once per overlapping 60 s trial window, about five copies of each (7221 stored trial-start events for 1412 distinct ones), and its event times are not sorted. The Plexon units table's spike times are not sorted either.

The trial tags are all "initial cue display" and carry no trial type. Reward size and outcome can be rebuilt from the events, and they then match the paper's Zenodo trial lists except trial 1411, which the events mark as a successful large reward trial and the list leaves out.

The paper says the reward size depends on whether the target is at the top or bottom of the screen. The events code left and right conditions, and both reward sizes occur on both sides, so the target position that sets the reward is not in the dandiset.

The raw FSCV minute files are joined without their gaps (328 min of scans against 302 min of trials, placed from a single starting time), and the trial-aligned oxidation current cannot be located in them, so the raw FSCV's clock could not be established.

Only one session of monkey T is deposited. The data behind the electrode yields, cultures, drainage volumes and bone growth, and all of monkey J, are not, so eight of the thirteen claims cannot be tested.

entries.title: Grid, head-direction and conjunctive cells by entorhinal layer (Sargolini et al. 2006)
entries.description: Tests three conclusions of Sargolini et al. (2006) on dandiset 000582, which holds spike times and tracked positions for 620 cell-sessions from the medial entorhinal cortex of 15 rats. For every cell it computes a grid score, head-direction tuning and speed tuning, with chance levels from time-shifted spike trains, and compares the cell types found in each cortical layer.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Sargolini et al. (2006) from dandiset 000582

entries.name: 000625-geiller-2020
entries.title: Molecularly identified CA1 interneurons during random foraging (Geiller, Vancura et al. 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Geiller, Vancura et al. (2020) that can be tested on dandiset 000625, which holds three random-foraging sessions of one mouse with 231 interneurons, 74 of them assigned one of the paper's six subtypes. It checks the imaging clock against the behaviour, then measures each interneuron's correlation with running speed, run-stop responses, spatial selectivity, position decoding and the stability of tuning curves within and across sessions. The sharp-wave ripple, novel-context, goal-oriented learning and VIP experiments are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Geiller, Vancura et al. (2020) from dandiset 000625

entries.name: 000691-scherrer-2023
entries.title: Imaging thousands of neurons in a freely moving mouse with a large-FOV head-mounted microscope (Scherrer et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Scherrer, Lynch, Zhang and Fee (2023) that can be tested on dandiset 000691, which holds one session of one mouse imaged with the large-FOV head-mounted microscope while it explores a looped maze, with 2948 EXTRACT footprints and a behaviour video. It counts the footprints, tracks the mouse from the video, decodes its position and direction from the activity, maps local decoding across the field of view, looks for footprints with localized activity and for the spread of coactive populations, and tests the illumination profiles of Extended Data Fig. 2 on images in the paper's code repository. The other mice, the birds and the optical tests are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Scherrer et al. (2023) from dandiset 000691

entries.name: 000718-zaki-2024
entries.title: Offline ensemble co-reactivation in the EEG/EMG experiment (Zaki et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Zaki et al. (2024) that can be tested on dandiset 000718, which holds two of the nine mice of the paper's calcium imaging and EEG/EMG experiment (one high-shock, one low-shock) with their encoding and recall sessions, the first offline recording after encoding, and cell registration for the high-shock mouse. It checks the deposited freezing against the paper's per-mouse values, compares freezing between the two mice, tests offline population bursts and their skew against shuffled activity and against movement, and compares overlap-neutral with overlap-aversive co-bursting in wake. The one-hour offline, behaviour-only, inhibitory tagging and no-shock experiments are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Zaki et al. (2024) from dandiset 000718

entries.name: 000727-brezovec-2022
entries.title: Brain-wide neural correlates of walking in Drosophila (Brezovec et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Brezovec, Berger, Druckmann and Clandinin (2022) on dandiset 000727, which holds whole-brain two-photon imaging and ball tracking of nine walking flies. It streams 12 planes of the authors' processed volumes in the Functional Drosophila Atlas for all flies, and tests the voxel correlations with forward and turning velocity, their symmetry, the principal components and the models that predict velocity from them, the demixing of velocity components, and the timing of neural activity relative to behaviour. Region-level results cannot be tested, as the dandiset has no neuropil labels.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Brezovec et al. (2022) from dandiset 000727

entries.name: 000947-schwab-2020
entries.title: GPi and VLa activity during reaching in macaques (Schwab et al. 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Schwab, Kase, Zimnik, Rosenbaum, Codianni, Rubin and Turner (2020) on the pre-MPTP recordings of dandiset 000947, single units from the internal globus pallidus and the ventrolateral anterior thalamus of two monkeys performing a reaching task. It compares rates, spike widths, peri-movement responses and their latencies, spike and rate correlations of simultaneously recorded pairs, and the effect of GPi bursts and pauses on VLa activity, and links the dandiset's units to the paper's own unit list.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Schwab et al. (2020) from dandiset 000947

entries.name: 000971-seiler-2022
entries.title: Dorsomedial striatal dopamine and compulsive reward seeking (Seiler et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Seiler, Cosme, Sherathiya, Schaid, Bianco, Bridgemohan and Lerner (2022) on dandiset 000971, which holds the operant behavior of a fiber photometry cohort and three optogenetic cohorts, dual-site photometry from DMS and DLS dopamine axons during RI60 and RR20 training, and western blot images. It tests the shock probe phenotypes and their behavior, the DMS and DLS rewarded-unrewarded peak scores, and the effects of DMS and DLS terminal manipulations. RI30 and shock probe photometry, fear conditioning, open field and histology are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Seiler et al. (2022) from dandiset 000971

entries.name: 001038-azcorra-2023
entries.title: Functional responses of genetic subtypes of dopamine neurons (Azcorra, Gaertner et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the fiber photometry findings of Azcorra, Gaertner et al. (2023) on dandiset 001038, which holds the recordings from striatal axons and SNc somas of Vglut2, Calb1, Anxa1, Aldh1a1 and DAT mice running on a treadmill and receiving rewards and air puffs. It covers locomotion signaling (Figures 2, 3 and 5), reward and air puff responses (Figure 4), clustering (Figure 6), soma and axon correlation (Figure 7) and Extended Data Figures 1 and 6 to 9. Two snRNA-seq claims of Figure 1 are tested on the paper's GEO matrices.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Azcorra, Gaertner et al. (2023) from dandiset 001038

entries.name: 001075-randi-2023
entries.title: Neural signal propagation atlas of C. elegans (Randi et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Randi, Sharma, Dvali and Leifer (2023) on dandiset 001075, which holds the 113 wild-type-background recordings of whole-brain calcium imaging during single-neuron optogenetic stimulation, 110 of them with extracted traces. It checks the recordings, the number of measured neuron pairs, three example connections of Figure 1, the spatial specificity of the stimulation, the responses to RID stimulation in WT and, from the paper's OSF export, in unc-31 animals, and how the per-pair measurements and recordings link to the paper's Source Data and OSF export. The q values, the spontaneous recordings and the kernel analyses are not testable.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Randi et al. (2023) from dandiset 001075

entries.name: 001084-vu-2024
entries.title: Striatal dopamine release patterns and targeted stimulation through micro-fiber arrays (Vu et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Vu, Brown, Wen et al. (2024) on dandiset 001084, which holds multi-fiber photometry from mice with arrays of 30 to 103 fibers across the striatum. It re-runs the paper's GLM of dopamine release to light and tone in 280 fibers of 7 mice (amplitude maps, latencies and their spatial gradients), the isosbestic controls, the D1 calcium correlations, the chronic reward responses, and the spread of release evoked by single-fiber stimulation with its controls. The freely moving, histology and jaw movement data of Figures 3, 7 and S1 are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Vu et al. (2024) from dandiset 001084

entries.name: 001097-liu-2024
entries.title: A hypothalamic line attractor for female mating (Liu, Nair et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Liu, Nair et al. (2024) on dandiset 001097, which holds miniscope imaging of VMHvl alpha-cells in female mice during mating, with annotations of male and female behaviour. It tests the behavioural dynamics of mating, single-cell tuning, GLM fits and persistence, and, with the authors' deposited rSLDS weights for two mice, how the receptive-day integration dimension and its cells behave across the oestrus cycle. Claims that need new rSLDS fits are blocked, as the model cannot be built or fit within the registry's environment and time limit.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Liu, Nair et al. (2024) from dandiset 001097

entries.name: 001170-ling-2023
entries.title: ON and OFF odor responses in the mouse olfactory bulb and locust antennal lobe (Ling et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Ling, Moss, Smith, Deng, Kroeger, Reimer, Raman and Arenkiel (bioRxiv 2023, v2 2024) on dandiset 001170, which holds two-photon imaging of olfactory bulb glomeruli in awake mice, seven sessions from four mice under the paper's block protocol and five random-order sessions. It compares glomerular ON and OFF responses, contrast enhancement between sequential odors, and odor classification after offset, and tests the locust findings on the recordings the paper deposited on Figshare.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Ling et al. (2023) from dandiset 001170

entries.name: 001172-lohani-2022
entries.title: Cholinergic and calcium dynamics across behavioural states (Lohani, Moberly et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Lohani, Moberly et al. (2022) on dandiset 001172, which holds dual-colour mesoscopic imaging of ACh3.0 and jRCaMP1b with face video, pupil and wheel data from 4 of the paper's 6 mice. It tests the regression of both signals on behaviour, transients at face movement and locomotion onsets, amplitudes in sustained states, and the state dependence of correlations between areas and between the two signals, using the Allen parcel masks of the paper's code. ECoG, pharmacology, control mice and cholinergic axon imaging are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Lohani, Moberly et al. (2022) from dandiset 001172

entries.name: 001453-fouke-2025
entries.title: Optomotor swimming of zebrafish and Danionella cerebrum (Fouke et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the freely swimming findings of Fouke, He, Loring and Naumann (2025) on dandiset 001453, which holds the tracking data of 25 zebrafish and 12 Danionella cerebrum larvae during the optomotor protocol. It compares swimming speed, turning and angular acceleration between species and stimuli, the response to monocular stimuli, and how steady the swimming is. The imaging and head-fixed tail tracking of the paper's Figures 2 to 4 are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Fouke et al. (2025) from dandiset 001453

entries.name: 001528-hadjas-2025
entries.title: Responses of SNr GABA and SNc dopamine neuron subtypes to STN and PPN input (Hadjas et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the mouse fiber photometry findings of Hadjas et al. (2025) on dandiset 001528, which holds recordings from 120 mice during optogenetic stimulation of STN or PPN inputs to the substantia nigra. It compares responses of SNr GABA neurons, SNc pan-DA neurons, striatal dopamine release in TS and DLS, DA terminals, and Vglut2+ and Anxa1+ DA neurons across train durations and frequencies, using the lab's dF/F stored in the files. The human tissue counts of Figure 1 are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Hadjas et al. (2025) from dandiset 001528

entries.name: 001538-zhai-2025
entries.title: State-dependent modulation of spiny projection neurons in levodopa-induced dyskinesia (Zhai et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Zhai, Cui, Wokosin, Sun, Tkatch, Crittenden, Graybiel and Surmeier (2025) on dandiset 001538. It measures somatic excitability (rheobase and spike counts) and the dendritic excitability index of dSPNs and iSPNs in the LID off- and on-states and under D1R, D2R and M1R antagonists, CDGI deletion and M1R deletion, and evoked ACh release with GRAB-ACh3.0. It links the recordings to the paper's per-cell tables on Zenodo. The Sr2+-oEPSC, ACh and AIM data hold too few cells or mice for most of the paper's tests, and the spine data are raw stacks only.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Zhai et al. (2025) from dandiset 001538

entries.name: 001550-pagan-2025
entries.title: Context-dependent evidence accumulation in rats (Pagan et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Pagan, Tang, Aoi, Pillow, Mante, Sussillo and Brody (2025) on dandiset 001550, which holds the behaviour of 26 rats trained on a task that switches between accumulating location and frequency evidence. It links the dandiset to the paper's published behavioural tables, checks the session statistics and selection, fits the behavioural pulse kernels and their slope indices, tests the optogenetic inactivation, and, with the paper's neural data from GitHub, the link between behavioural and neural slope indices.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Pagan et al. (2025) from dandiset 001550

entries.name: 001616-gerken-2025
entries.title: Single units of the human medial temporal lobe during a full-length movie (Gerken, Darcher et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Gerken, Darcher et al. (eLife reviewed preprint 106758, 2025) on dandiset 001616 (SUMMER), which holds 2286 units from 29 patients watching "500 Days of Summer" with 53 frame-wise annotations. It counts units responsive to the onsets of movie features, runs the cluster permutation test by region, and decodes characters, location and cuts with the paper's logistic regression, pooled, per patient, per region and on subsets of units. The paper's LSTM is not run.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Gerken, Darcher et al. (2025) from dandiset 001616
Top-ranked units for decoding Summer (Figure 7)

Responsive units by the dataset code's ZETA test, character, person and location labels (variant)

entries.name: 001636-pasquereau-2013
entries.title: M1 responses to muscle stretch in the parkinsonian monkey (Pasquereau and Turner 2013)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Pasquereau and Turner (2013) on dandiset 001636, which holds single-unit recordings from M1 of two monkeys before and after MPTP, with torque perturbations, joint angle and EMG. Only monkey V can be tested, as the monkey L files mark no perturbation. The notebook checks the cells, resting rates and antidromic latencies, detects torque responses, and compares the torque-evoked movements and triceps EMG before and after MPTP.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Pasquereau and Turner (2013) from dandiset 001636

entries.name: 001692-bouabid-2026
entries.title: Striatal dopamine-acetylcholine hotspot (Bouabid, Vu et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Bouabid, Vu et al. (2026) on dandiset 001692, which holds multi-fiber photometry of dopamine and acetylcholine across the striatum of 17 mice. It reproduces the spontaneous cross-correlations and their anterior dorsolateral hotspot, paired transients, reward, Pavlovian cue, locomotion and optogenetic stimulation analyses, and the control mice, and tests the ex vivo slice statistics of Figure 8 on the paper's source data on Zenodo.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Bouabid, Vu et al. (2026) from dandiset 001692

entries.name: 001699-moore-2025
entries.title: Head-direction coding in juvenile and adult Fmr1-/y rats (Moore et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Moore, Duszkiewicz, Asiminas, Dudchenko, Peyrache and Wood (bioRxiv 2025) on dandiset 001699, which holds silicon-probe recordings of the postsubiculum of 24 juvenile and adult Fmr1-/y and wild-type rats during open-field exploration and sleep. It recomputes the cell selection, head-direction tuning, its stability within and between sessions, decoder drift, and tuning to the Isomap angle of waking and REM population activity, and compares genotypes in each age group.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Moore et al. (2025) from dandiset 001699

entries.name: 001712-davatolhagh-2025
entries.title: Prior use and cortical dynamics in a Nrxn1a mouse model (Davatolhagh et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Davatolhagh et al. (2025) that can be tested on dandiset 001712, which holds one widefield imaging and behaviour session of one mouse of unstated genotype in the IBL biased choice task. It tests the psychometric curve, reaction times, the use of the block prior, adaptation after block switches, lateralized visual responses and a linear encoding model of the imaging with task and movement predictors. The comparisons between knockout and wild-type mice cannot be tested.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Davatolhagh et al. (2025) from dandiset 001712
Encoding model with the video components of all three cameras (variant)

entries.name: 001754-knierim-2000
entries.title: Place cells during space flight on the Neurolab mission (Knierim et al. 2000)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Knierim, McNaughton and Poe (2000) that can be tested on dandiset 001754, which holds sorted units, task epochs, rate maps and spike-time positions of three rats recorded before and during the Neurolab shuttle mission. It tests spatial selectivity on the Escher staircase in flight, spatial information in flight against preflight, and the stability of place fields across two sessions. The paper is not open access; claims come from its abstract, its figure titles and the dandiset's description. There is no EEG in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Knierim et al. (2000) from dandiset 001754

entries.name: 001878-sun-2021
entries.title: CalMS21 mouse social behavior dataset (Sun et al. 2021)
entries.description: Tests the claims of Sun et al. (2021), the paper describing the CalMS21 dataset of resident-intruder pose and behavior annotations, on dandiset 001878, which holds one CalMS21 sequence (Task 1 test sequence mouse071) with its video, and on the full dataset deposited on CaltechDATA. It checks the format, identities and annotations of the dandiset's sequence, links it to the deposit, and tests the dataset's counts and label fractions. The model benchmarks are not run.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Sun et al. (2021) from dandiset 001878 and the CalMS21 deposit

entries.name: 001888-hristova-2025
entries.title: Absence seizures and sleep in Grin2b+/- rats (Hristova, Fasol et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the EEG findings of Hristova, Fasol et al. (2025) on dandiset 001888, which holds the 24-h wireless EEG and EMG recordings, sleep scores and SWD events of 14 Grin2b+/- rats, 2 wild type rats and one rat without genotype. It compares SWD number, duration and timing, sleep-wake amounts and bouts, state spectra computed from the raw EEG, the state in which SWDs start, and the correlation of SWD time with sleep measures. The western blots, development measures, visual scoring and pharmacology recordings of the paper are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Hristova, Fasol et al. (2025) from dandiset 001888

entries.name: 001933-chen-2026
entries.title: LRRK2-G2019S and dopamine release from Anxa1+ and Calb1+ neurons (Chen, He et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Chen, He et al. (2026). On dandiset 001933, which holds GRAB-DA3m fiber photometry in the dorsal striatum during optogenetic stimulation of Anxa1+ (15 mice) or Calb1+ (12 mice) SNc dopamine neurons in LRRK2-WT and LRRK2-G2019S mice, it compares evoked and spontaneous dopamine release between genotypes, per power and per mouse, and links the dandiset to the paper's published source data. The imaging, proteomics and western blots of Figures 1 to 5 are not in the dandiset; their claims are tested on the data the paper deposited on Zenodo, in PRIDE and in the BioImage Archive, and counted apart.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Chen, He et al. (2026) from dandiset 001933

entries.name: 002013-amjad-2025
entries.title: Microinvasive probes for dopamine, LFP and spikes in monkeys (Amjad et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Amjad, Mahajan, Choi, Shrivastav, Murray, Somich, Coyne and Schwerdt (2025) on dandiset 002013, which holds the three example sessions of the paper. It checks the recording parameters and task structure, the dopamine response to large and small reward cues at site c8dg, beta-band LFP suppression by reward and cue side at c3bs-c3a, beta bursts around the cue, and the isolation of the sorted unit of monkey P, and compares the dandiset with the paper's Zenodo deposit.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Amjad et al. (2025) from dandiset 002013

entries.name: 002014-choi-2025
entries.title: Dopamine, spikes and LFP through an aseptic cranial chamber in a rhesus monkey (Choi et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the recording findings of Choi et al. (2025) on dandiset 002014, which holds one session of monkey T recorded through the paper's semi-sealed chamber. It compares dopamine and beta-band LFP power between large and small reward trials, aligns spikes to the value cue, and checks the unit's waveform and interspike intervals. The surgical, culture, drainage and yield results, and monkey J, are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Choi et al. (2025) from dandiset 002014
